This memorandum summarizes the renewal review conducted for the vendor agreement between Halden Ridge Logistics Corporation and Braxton-Miller Supply Solutions, covering the period of the upcoming contract term beginning March 1 and extending through the following twenty-four months. The review was completed by the Procurement Standards Committee in coordination with the Vendor Relations office, with input solicited from the Operations and Finance departments given the scope of services provided under the current agreement. The purpose of this document is to consolidate findings from the renewal assessment, outline the negotiated terms, and provide a record for internal reference should questions arise during the audit cycle scheduled for the third quarter.

Braxton-Miller Supply Solutions has served as the primary vendor for warehouse packaging materials and related consumables since the original agreement was executed under the tenure of former Procurement Director Elaine Ostrowski. The relationship has been characterized by consistent delivery performance, with only minor deviations noted in the quarterly service logs, most of which were attributed to regional transportation disruptions rather than vendor error. Over the past contract cycle, Braxton-Miller supplied an average of 4,200 units of corrugated packaging stock per month to the Halden Ridge distribution center located in Fennimore, along with ancillary items such as strapping tape, pallet wrap, and moisture-control packets. Invoicing accuracy remained within acceptable tolerances throughout the period, with a discrepancy rate below the two percent threshold established in the original service level agreement.

During the renewal negotiation, representatives from both organizations met on three separate occasions to review pricing structures, delivery schedules, and quality assurance provisions. The initial meeting was held on January 9 and included Procurement Manager Dennis Ferraro on behalf of Halden Ridge and Account Executive Priya Nandakumar representing Braxton-Miller. Subsequent sessions on January 22 and February 3 addressed specific line-item adjustments, including a modest increase in per-unit pricing for packaging materials to reflect rising costs of raw cardboard stock, which the vendor attributed to broader market conditions affecting the paper products industry. Halden Ridge's Finance team, led by Controller Marguerite Solheim, reviewed the proposed pricing changes and determined that the adjustment, amounting to a 3.4 percent increase across the affected product categories, remained within budgetary parameters established for the upcoming fiscal year.

In addition to pricing, the renewed agreement incorporates several modifications to the original terms. The delivery window has been adjusted from a standard five-business-day turnaround to a four-business-day turnaround for standard orders, reflecting improvements in Braxton-Miller's regional distribution network following the opening of their new fulfillment facility in Cedarbrook. Rush order provisions remain unchanged, with a 48-hour expedited delivery option available at an additional surcharge of 12 percent above standard pricing. The parties also agreed to formalize a quarterly business review process, which had previously occurred on an informal basis, to ensure consistent communication regarding forecasted volume needs, seasonal demand fluctuations, and any emerging supply chain concerns that could affect service continuity.

The renewed contract also updates the insurance and liability provisions to align with Halden Ridge's revised vendor risk management policy, which was adopted company-wide following a broader compliance review conducted last year. Braxton-Miller has confirmed that its general liability coverage meets the updated minimum threshold of two million dollars per occurrence, and documentation verifying this coverage has been submitted to the Vendor Compliance office and filed accordingly. No changes were required to the indemnification clauses, as the existing language was found to satisfy current legal requirements upon review by outside counsel retained for this purpose.

Performance metrics from the prior term were factored into the renewal decision, with particular attention paid to the vendor scorecard maintained by the Operations department. Braxton-Miller achieved an overall performance rating of 4.2 out of 5 across the evaluated categories, which include on-time delivery, order accuracy, responsiveness to inquiries, and issue resolution timeliness. The lowest-scoring category was responsiveness to inquiries, where average response times to non-urgent requests occasionally exceeded the 24-hour benchmark outlined in the service agreement. Vendor Relations has requested that Braxton-Miller designate an additional point of contact to help address this gap, and the vendor has agreed to assign a secondary account representative, Colin Whitfield, who will support Ms. Nandakumar in managing day-to-day communications going forward.

Budgetary implications of the renewal were reviewed by the Finance department, and it was determined that the overall increase in projected spend, accounting for both the pricing adjustment and anticipated volume growth tied to the planned expansion of the Fennimore distribution center, falls within the range anticipated during the annual budget planning process. No additional budget approval beyond existing departmental authority was deemed necessary, though Finance recommended that spend against this contract be monitored on a quarterly basis alongside the newly implemented business review meetings.

Based on the findings summarized above, the Procurement Standards Committee recommends proceeding with the renewal under the terms outlined in this document. The finalized agreement is pending signature from both parties, with execution anticipated before the current contract's expiration date to avoid any lapse in service. A copy of the fully executed agreement, along with supporting documentation, will be retained in the vendor file maintained by the Procurement Standards Committee and made available for reference during future audit or review cycles. Any questions regarding this summary or the underlying negotiation process may be directed to the Vendor Relations office for clarification.

Ticket #48213-A
Account: Meridian Logistics Group
Contact: Denise Ferrow, Operations Coordinator
Priority: Standard
Product: Hallstrom WMS, Warehouse Management Suite v4.2
Assigned Agent: Carl Nyquist, Tier 2 Support

Initial Submission (09:14 AM, Tuesday)
Customer reports that the batch import function within the Hallstrom WMS inventory module has been returning intermittent timeout errors when uploading files larger than 15,000 line items. Denise Ferrow noted that the issue began after the most recent system update was applied on Monday evening. She stated that three separate attempts were made to upload the weekly inventory reconciliation file, all of which failed at approximately the same point in the process, roughly seventy percent through the upload bar. No error code was displayed, only a generic message reading "Process could not be completed. Please try again later." Denise requested a callback within the standard four-hour window as outlined in the Meridian service agreement.

Agent Response (09:47 AM, Tuesday)
Carl Nyquist acknowledged the ticket and requested additional information, including the exact file size in megabytes, the file format being used (CSV versus XLSX), and whether the issue occurred on a single workstation or across multiple terminals within the Meridian facility. Carl also asked whether any antivirus or firewall software had been recently updated on the affected machines, as this has historically been a contributing factor in similar cases logged under other accounts. Denise was asked to confirm the browser and version in use, since the WMS portal is primarily accessed through a web interface for the import function.

Customer Follow-Up (11:02 AM, Tuesday)
Denise responded that the file in question was a CSV export, approximately 42 megabytes, and that the issue had been reproduced on two separate terminals, one running Chrome version 118 and another running Edge version 117. She confirmed that no changes had been made to antivirus software on either machine in the past thirty days. She attached a screenshot of the error message as requested and noted that the file had previously uploaded without issue prior to Monday's update.

Agent Response (11:35 AM, Tuesday)
Carl thanked Denise for the additional detail and escalated the ticket internally to the engineering team responsible for the update rollout, flagging it as a potential regression issue tied to the batch processing service. He informed Denise that a root cause analysis would be initiated and that an estimated response time of one business day should be expected for a preliminary finding. In the interim, Carl suggested that Denise attempt to split the file into smaller batches of approximately 5,000 line items each as a temporary workaround, noting that this approach had resolved similar timeout issues for other clients in the past when larger files were involved.

Customer Follow-Up (02:18 PM, Tuesday)
Denise reported that splitting the file into smaller batches did allow the uploads to complete successfully, though she noted this added a meaningful amount of manual work to her team's daily reconciliation process and was not a sustainable long-term solution. She asked whether the engineering team could provide a target date for a permanent fix and requested that the ticket remain open until resolution was confirmed.

Internal Note (03:40 PM, Tuesday)

This memorandum summarizes the renewal review of the master services agreement between Halden Cooperative Distribution and its logistics software provider, Corrivale Systems Inc., originally executed on March 4, 2021, and set to expire on June 30 of this year. The purpose of this document is to consolidate the findings of the procurement team, outline the negotiated terms for the renewal period, and provide a record for internal audit purposes regarding the continuation of services under a modified fee structure.

The current agreement covers the licensing of Corrivale's warehouse management platform, branded internally as the Meridian Suite, which Halden Cooperative Distribution has used across its four regional fulfillment centers since the initial rollout in the second quarter of 2021. Over the past contract term, the platform has been used to manage inbound receiving, inventory allocation, and outbound shipment scheduling for approximately sixty percent of the company's total order volume. Support tickets logged through the vendor portal averaged eleven per month, with an average resolution time of forty-two hours, which falls within the service level agreement threshold of seventy-two hours specified in Section 6.2 of the original contract. No major service interruptions were recorded during the term, though there were two instances of scheduled maintenance extending beyond the posted window, both of which were addressed through service credits applied to the November and January invoices respectively.

Following a review conducted by the procurement and operations teams in April, it was determined that renewal of the agreement remains the preferred course of action over transitioning to an alternative vendor. The review committee, comprising representatives Marcus Ilford from Operations, Denise Okafor from Finance, and Tomas Bregman from IT Infrastructure, evaluated three competing proposals from alternative software providers, including Larkspur Analytics and Fennimore Logistics Technologies, but concluded that the switching costs associated with data migration and staff retraining would outweigh the marginal savings offered by competitors. Additionally, the existing integration between the Meridian Suite and Halden's internal accounting system, maintained by the finance department, was cited as a significant factor favoring continuity, given the substantial internal investment already made in customizing that integration over the prior contract term.

The renewed agreement, effective July 1, extends the term for an additional twenty-four months, through June 30 two years hence, with an option for a further twelve-month extension subject to mutual written consent no later than ninety days prior to expiration. The annual licensing fee has been adjusted from its previous rate of one hundred eighty-four thousand dollars to one hundred ninety-six thousand dollars, reflecting a six and a half percent increase attributed to expanded user seat allocations and the addition of two modules not included in the original scope, specifically the predictive replenishment module and the carrier rate comparison tool. These additions were requested by the operations team following a needs assessment conducted last autumn, which identified recurring manual workarounds that the new modules are expected to eliminate.

Payment terms remain net thirty days from invoice date, with invoicing to occur quarterly rather than the previous semiannual schedule, a change requested by Halden's finance department to improve cash flow forecasting alignment with internal budgeting cycles. Corrivale Systems has agreed to maintain the existing service level commitments without modification, including the seventy-two-hour resolution window for standard support tickets and a four-hour response window for critical system outages classified as Severity One incidents. The renewed contract also incorporates an updated data processing addendum reflecting recent changes to regional data privacy regulations, which was reviewed by outside counsel, Gwendolyn Farraday of Alder & Whitcombe LLP, prior to execution.

A notable addition to the renewed terms is a provision for an annual business review meeting, to be held each January, during which representatives from both organizations will assess platform performance metrics, discuss upcoming feature roadmaps, and identify opportunities for further process optimization. This provision was proposed by Halden's operations team in response to feedback that communication with the vendor had historically been reactive rather than proactive, occurring primarily in response to support issues rather than as part of ongoing strategic planning.

Training for the two new modules will be conducted over a six-week period beginning in mid-July, with Corrivale providing on-site training sessions at the Northfield and Cascade Ridge distribution centers, supplemented by virtual sessions for staff at the remaining two facilities. The rollout schedule has been coordinated with the operations calendar to avoid overlap with the peak shipping period typically observed in late summer, in order to minimize disruption to daily fulfillment operations.

Budget approval for the renewed contract was obtained from the finance committee during its May meeting, with the increased annual fee incorporated into the fiscal year budget under the existing technology services line item. No additional capital expenditure approval was required, as the arrangement continues to be structured as a subscription-based licensing model rather than a capital purchase. The contract has been signed by authorized representatives from both organizations, with Halden Cooperative Distribution represented by Chief Operations Officer Priya Adebayo and Corrivale Systems Inc. represented by Regional Account Director Nathaniel Voss.

This summary will be retained in the vendor management file alongside the executed agreement and supporting exhibits, and copies have been distributed to the finance, operations, and IT infrastructure departments for their records. Any questions regarding the terms outlined above should be directed to the procurement team for clarification prior to the next scheduled review cycle.

Prepared by the Product Management Office, Meridian Softworks Inc., this document outlines the requirements for the upcoming release of the Comet Ledger module within the company's existing Aurora Financial Suite. The project sponsor is Denise Halbrook, Vice President of Product, and the primary author is Trent Okafor, Senior Product Manager, with contributions from the engineering leads Priya Ramaswamy and Callum Bester. This version supersedes the draft circulated on March 4th and incorporates feedback gathered during the stakeholder review session held in the Beacon Hill conference room on March 18th.

The purpose of the Comet Ledger module is to provide mid-sized accounting firms with a streamlined reconciliation workflow that reduces the manual effort currently required to match transactions across multiple client accounts. Feedback from our customer advisory board, composed of representatives from Alden & Pruitt Bookkeeping, Northfield Tax Partners, and Ruskin Associates, indicates that reconciliation tasks presently consume an average of six hours per week per staff accountant, largely due to the lack of automated matching rules and the absence of a centralized exception queue. The business objective of this release is to reduce that average to under two hours per week within the first two quarters following launch, while maintaining the accuracy standards already certified under our SOC 2 compliance framework.

The scope of this release includes four primary capabilities. First, an automated matching engine that compares bank statement line items against ledger entries using configurable tolerance thresholds for amount and date variance. Second, an exception queue interface that surfaces unmatched or partially matched transactions for manual review, sorted by dollar value and age. Third, a rules configuration panel that allows firm administrators to define custom matching logic without requiring engineering support, including the ability to save and reuse rule sets across client engagements. Fourth, an audit trail feature that logs every automated and manual match decision, timestamped and attributed to the responsible user, in order to satisfy existing regulatory recordkeeping requirements referenced in our compliance addendum, document C-114.

Out of scope for this release are integrations with third-party payroll systems, support for multi-currency reconciliation, and any changes to the existing invoicing module. These items have been logged in the backlog under the Comet Ledger Phase Two initiative and will be evaluated for prioritization following the completion of this release. The product team has deliberately narrowed scope to ensure the core matching and exception-handling functionality is delivered on schedule and can be validated thoroughly before additional complexity is introduced.

From a user perspective, the primary persona for this release is the staff accountant, typically responsible for reconciling between three and fifteen client accounts on a weekly or biweekly basis. A secondary persona is the firm administrator, who configures matching rules and periodically reviews audit logs for compliance purposes. User research conducted by Meridian's research analyst, Owen Fitzgerald, through structured interviews with eleven accountants across four partner firms, indicated a strong preference for a queue-based interface over the current spreadsheet export workflow, as well as a desire for visual indicators distinguishing high-confidence matches from those requiring manual attention.

Functional requirements are as follows. The matching engine must process a minimum of ten thousand transaction pairs within thirty seconds on standard production hardware, consistent with the performance benchmarks established for other modules in the Aurora suite. The exception queue must support filtering by client account, transaction date range, and dollar amount, and must allow bulk actions such as marking multiple transactions as resolved simultaneously. The rules configuration panel must validate rule syntax in real time and prevent administrators from saving conflicting or redundant rules. The audit trail must be exportable in both CSV and PDF formats to accommodate firms that undergo periodic third-party audits.

Non-functional requirements include a target page load time of under two seconds for the exception queue interface under typical usage conditions, and system availability consistent with our existing service level agreement of 99.5 percent uptime measured monthly. Security requirements mandate that all transaction data remain encrypted at rest and in transit, consistent with existing Aurora suite standards, and that access to the audit trail be restricted based on role-based permissions already defined in the identity management system maintained by the infrastructure team under Marcus Delaney's direction.

The proposed release timeline anticipates a closed beta beginning in the second week of May, involving three of the four advisory board firms, followed by a general availability release targeted for the final week of June, pending successful completion of user acceptance testing. The engineering team estimates the development effort at approximately eleven person-weeks, with an additional three person-weeks allocated for quality assurance and regression testing across the broader Aurora suite to confirm that existing modules remain unaffected.

Success will be measured through a combination of quantitative and qualitative indicators. Quantitatively, the product team will track the average time spent per reconciliation session, the percentage of transactions automatically matched without manual intervention, and the rate of exception queue resolution within a rolling seven-day window. Qualitatively, the team will conduct follow-up interviews with beta participants approximately four weeks after launch to assess satisfaction and identify any friction points not captured through analytics alone.

This document will be reviewed again prior to the beta launch to incorporate any adjustments arising from engineering estimation sessions or additional stakeholder feedback. Questions or comments regarding this document should be directed to Trent Okafor via the Product Management distribution list, and any proposed changes to scope must be approved by Denise Halbrook prior to implementation.

From: Marlene Ostrowski
To: Project Meridian Distribution List
Subject: RE: Meridian Phase 2 Status - Week of March 10

All,

Following up on last week's steering committee call, I wanted to circulate a consolidated status update on Phase 2 of the Meridian data migration effort before our Thursday checkpoint. As most of you know, we completed the schema validation pass on the Hartwell warehouse dataset last Tuesday, and QA has now signed off on the first two of the four target tables. The remaining two tables, CUSTOMER_LEDGER and TXN_HISTORY_ARCHIVE, are still pending validation due to some inconsistencies in the timestamp formatting that Priya's team flagged on the 6th.

Priya, can you confirm whether the timestamp normalization script from Dennis is expected to resolve those inconsistencies, or if we need to loop in the vendor (Corvale Systems) for a patch? I know we discussed this briefly on the standup call, but I want to make sure we have something concrete to report to Bill Ashworth before the exec review on the 21st.

On the infrastructure side, the staging environment upgrade that Tom's team completed last Friday appears stable. We ran a load test over the weekend simulating roughly 1.4x our expected peak volume, and response times stayed within the SLA thresholds we agreed on with Operations back in January. Tom, if you could send over the full load test report when you get a chance, that would be appreciated - I'd like to attach it to the steering committee packet rather than just summarizing it verbally.

Lastly, a reminder that the change freeze for the downstream reporting systems begins March 24th and runs through April 2nd to accommodate the fiscal quarter close. Anyone with dependencies that touch the reporting layer should plan around that window. Let me know if there are conflicts.

Thanks,
Marlene

---

From: Priya Anand
To: Marlene Ostrowski; Project Meridian Distribution List
Subject: RE: Meridian Phase 2 Status - Week of March 10

Marlene,

Thanks for the summary. On the timestamp issue - Dennis's normalization script handles about 92% of the malformed records we've seen so far, but there's a subset (roughly 3,000 rows out of the 340,000 we sampled) where the original source system appears to have written the timestamp in a locale-specific format that doesn't match anything in our conversion table. Dennis thinks these came from the legacy Brackenfield office before it was folded into the Ashcombe regional system in 2019, so the formatting is basically a historical artifact.

We're leaning toward manually mapping these edge cases rather than looping in Corvale, mostly because their last two patch turnarounds took over three weeks and we don't have that kind of runway before the 21st. Dennis estimates the manual mapping effort at about two days of work if we pull in one more analyst temporarily. I'd like to request that Greg free up Nadia for this from the Falkirk reporting team, since she's done similar cleanup work before on the Instrument Master project last year.

I'll have a firmer estimate by Wednesday morning. In the meantime, QA has agreed to proceed with validation on the other two tables in parallel so we're not blocked entirely.

Best,
Priya

---

From: Tom Reyes
To: Marlene Ostrowski; Project Meridian Distribution List
Subject: RE: Meridian Phase 2 Status - Week of March 10

Hi all,

Attaching the full load test report as requested. Quick summary for those who don't want to dig through all forty pages: average response time under simulated peak load was 340ms, with the 95th percentile at 610ms, both comfortably under our 800ms SLA ceiling. Memory utilization on the new staging cluster peaked at 71%, which gives us some headroom, though I'd like to revisit capacity planning once we have real production numbers post-cutover rather than relying solely on simulated load.

One thing worth flagging: during the test we noticed a minor issue with the connection pooling configuration on node three that caused a brief spike in latency around the 40-minute mark. It self-corrected and didn't affect overall test results, but I've asked Ravi to look into the pool sizing settings this week just to be safe. Nothing that should hold up the schedule, but wanted it on record.

Also, noting the change freeze dates - our team doesn't have any direct dependencies on the reporting layer during that window, but I know the Kestrel Analytics integration (owned by Sam's group) does pull from some of the same tables, so it might be worth a quick check with them separately.

Tom

---

This document describes the requirements for the Harborline Reporting Module, an internal-facing feature set to be integrated into the existing Meridian Insights platform. The purpose of Harborline is to address recurring customer feedback regarding the limitations of the current export and scheduling functionality within the reporting suite. Over the past three quarters, Customer Success has logged approximately two hundred and forty distinct support tickets referencing delays in report generation, inflexible scheduling windows, and an inability to customize recipient lists on a per-report basis. This document consolidates those findings into a set of prioritized requirements intended to guide the engineering team through a six-month development cycle, culminating in a general availability release targeted for the first week of March of next year.

The background for this initiative stems from a broader strategic decision made during the fall planning cycle to reduce customer churn attributable to reporting friction. Meridian Analytics Group has historically differentiated itself through its data visualization capabilities, but internal surveys conducted by the Customer Success team indicate that nearly a third of clients on the Professional and Enterprise tiers consider the reporting workflow to be a weak point relative to competitor offerings, notably those from Castlebrook Systems and Nordvale Data. Given that reporting is frequently cited during renewal conversations, the Product organization has classified this initiative as a top-three priority for the upcoming fiscal year.

The primary objective of the Harborline Reporting Module is to allow account administrators to configure automated report deliveries with greater granularity than is currently possible. At present, users may only schedule reports on a fixed daily, weekly, or monthly cadence, with delivery times constrained to a single global setting per organization. The new module must support custom scheduling intervals, including specific day-of-week combinations, time zone-aware delivery windows, and the ability to pause or resume a schedule without deleting the underlying configuration. Additionally, the module must allow administrators to designate different recipient groups for different reports, rather than relying on a single organization-wide distribution list, which has been a persistent source of complaint among clients managing multiple departments or business units.

A secondary objective involves improving the performance and reliability of report generation for large datasets. Engineering has identified that reports exceeding fifty thousand rows currently experience an average generation time of eleven minutes, which frequently exceeds the timeout threshold configured in certain client firewalls, resulting in failed deliveries that are not always retried automatically. The Harborline module must introduce a background processing queue with configurable retry logic, along with a notification mechanism that alerts the report owner when a delivery has failed after three consecutive attempts. This requirement was flagged as high priority by both Tom Iwasaki's engineering team and by Priya Chandrasekaran's Customer Success organization, given the reputational risk associated with silent failures.

In terms of scope, this release will focus exclusively on the scheduling and delivery mechanics of existing report types. It will not include the introduction of new visualization types, nor will it address the request, raised separately by several Enterprise clients, for embedded reporting within third-party dashboards such as those offered by Solandra Business Intelligence. That request has been logged separately as a candidate for a future initiative and is explicitly out of scope for this document. Similarly, this release will not modify the underlying data warehouse architecture, as any such changes are being handled independently by the Data Platform team under a separate roadmap led by Renata Vasquez.

From a functional requirements standpoint, the module must include an administrative interface accessible from the existing Settings panel, allowing designated users to view, edit, duplicate, and archive report schedules. Duplication is considered a required feature rather than a nice-to-have, as feedback from the Client Advisory Board, chaired this year by representatives from Bramwell Logistics and Corrigan Health Partners, indicated that clients frequently need to create near-identical schedules with minor variations in recipient lists or delivery times. The interface must also surface a delivery history log showing the status of the last ten delivery attempts per report, including timestamps and any error messages generated during failed attempts, to reduce the volume of support tickets requiring manual log inspection by engineering staff.

Non-functional requirements include a target uptime of 99.5 percent for the scheduling service, consistent with the existing service level agreement offered to Enterprise clients. The module must also comply with the data retention policies currently enforced across the Meridian platform, meaning that delivery logs older than ninety days should be automatically purged unless a client has opted into extended retention as part of a premium support agreement. Security review will be required prior to release, given that the recipient list functionality involves handling of email addresses that may be considered personally identifiable information under certain regional data protection regulations, and the Legal and Compliance team, represented by Marcus Delaney, has requested a formal sign-off meeting no later than six weeks before the planned release date.

Success for this initiative will be measured primarily through a reduction in reporting-related support tickets, with a target decrease of forty percent within two quarters of general availability, as well as through qualitative feedback gathered during the subsequent Client Advisory Board session. Additional metrics will include the average time to generate large reports, which Engineering aims to reduce to under four minutes, and the percentage of clients who adopt custom scheduling configurations within the first ninety days of release, targeted at twenty-five percent of eligible accounts. Progress against these metrics will be reviewed jointly by Product and Customer Success on a monthly basis following launch, with findings incorporated into the subsequent planning cycle.

This report summarizes the operational and financial performance of Meridian Fulfillment Solutions for the third quarter of the fiscal year, covering the period from July 1 through September 30. The purpose of this document is to provide the executive leadership team, department heads, and relevant board members with a consolidated view of business activity, departmental progress, and near-term outlook heading into the fourth quarter.

Overall revenue for the quarter came in at $14.2 million, representing a 4.6 percent increase over the previous quarter and a 9.1 percent increase year over year. This growth was driven primarily by continued expansion within the Regional Distribution division, which benefited from the onboarding of two new mid-sized retail clients, Halloway Home Goods and Corbin & Fitch Outfitters. Both accounts transitioned smoothly during the quarter, with implementation timelines meeting or exceeding internal targets. The Client Services team, led by Denise Okafor, reported that onboarding satisfaction scores for these accounts averaged 8.7 out of 10, slightly above the trailing four-quarter average of 8.3.

Operating expenses increased modestly, up 2.3 percent compared to Q2, largely attributable to seasonal staffing increases in the warehouse network ahead of the anticipated holiday volume ramp. The Logan Ridge and Pemberton distribution centers each added temporary headcount in September to prepare for projected Q4 throughput, and initial training completion rates at both sites exceeded 95 percent by quarter's end. Facilities and logistics costs remained largely in line with budget, though fuel surcharges from third-party carrier partners, including Ashcombe Freight Lines, contributed to a slight uptick in outbound shipping costs relative to forecast. Finance projects that these costs will stabilize in Q4 barring any significant disruption in regional fuel pricing.

The Technology division, under the direction of Priya Ramaswamy, continued work on the Horizon Warehouse Management upgrade, which remains on schedule for a phased rollout beginning in early Q1 of next fiscal year. During Q3, the team completed integration testing for the inventory reconciliation module and resolved several data synchronization issues that had been flagged during the previous quarter's pilot phase at the Delacroix facility. User acceptance testing is scheduled to begin in mid-October with a cohort of twelve warehouse supervisors across three sites. Management remains confident that the upgrade will meaningfully reduce manual reconciliation time once fully deployed, though the team has noted that additional budget may be required in Q4 to support extended vendor consulting hours related to the custom reporting dashboard.

Human Resources reported a relatively stable quarter with respect to workforce metrics. Voluntary turnover across the organization held at 11.2 percent on an annualized basis, consistent with Q2 and modestly below the industry benchmark cited in the most recent Meridian competitive analysis. The department completed its annual engagement survey during August, with a response rate of 78 percent across all locations. Preliminary results indicate continued strong scores in areas related to manager communication and role clarity, while scores related to career development opportunities remain an area identified for improvement. HR Director Marcus Whitfield has proposed a revised internal mobility program to be piloted in Q1, details of which will be presented to leadership in a separate memo prior to the next quarterly review.

Sales and Marketing activity during the quarter focused heavily on preparation for the upcoming Fall Logistics Conference in Denver, where Meridian will host a booth and participate in two panel discussions related to last-mile delivery optimization. The marketing team, working alongside outside vendor Cresthill Creative, finalized updated collateral and a refreshed presentation deck ahead of the event. Lead generation efforts during Q3 produced 214 qualified inquiries, a slight decrease from the 238 recorded in Q2, which the team attributes to typical summer seasonality rather than any structural shift in demand. Conversion rates on those inquiries remained consistent with historical averages at approximately 18 percent.

The Finance department completed its internal audit cycle for the quarter without material findings. Cash reserves remain healthy, with the company maintaining a current ratio of 2.1, comfortably within the range targeted by the board's finance committee. Accounts receivable aging showed a marginal increase in the 60-to-90-day bucket, primarily tied to delayed payments from one client account currently under review by the credit team; this matter is not considered a significant risk at this time but will continue to be monitored. Capital expenditures for the quarter totaled $612,000, largely allocated to warehouse equipment upgrades at the Ashfield facility and continued investment in the Horizon system rollout mentioned earlier in this report.

Looking ahead to the fourth quarter, leadership anticipates continued volume growth driven by seasonal demand and the full ramp-up of the two newly onboarded accounts. Operational priorities will include completing Horizon system testing, finalizing holiday staffing plans across all distribution centers, and continuing to monitor carrier cost trends given ongoing volatility in fuel pricing. The executive team will reconvene in early January to review full fiscal year results and finalize strategic priorities for the coming year, with a preliminary planning session tentatively scheduled for the second week of December pending calendar confirmation from all department heads.

In summary, Q3 performance reflects steady, controlled growth across most business lines, with no significant areas of concern identified during this reporting period. Departments are encouraged to continue current initiatives while remaining attentive to seasonal operational pressures as the organization moves into its historically busiest quarter of the year.

Section 7: Remote Work and Flexible Scheduling Policy

Meridian Analytics Group recognizes that the modern workplace has evolved to accommodate a variety of working arrangements that support both organizational needs and employee well-being. This policy outlines the guidelines and expectations governing remote work, hybrid schedules, and flexible hours for all eligible employees across the company's divisions, including the Client Services team, the Data Insights unit, and the Operations department. This policy applies to all full-time and part-time employees who have completed their initial ninety-day introductory period, unless otherwise specified by their direct supervisor or department head.

Eligibility for remote or hybrid work arrangements is determined on a role-by-role basis, taking into account the nature of the position, the employee's performance history, and the operational requirements of the team. Employees interested in pursuing a flexible work arrangement should submit a Flexible Work Request Form to their supervisor at least fourteen business days in advance of the desired start date. Supervisors are expected to review these requests in consultation with the Human Resources department, currently led by Regional HR Director Pamela Osei, and to provide a written response within ten business days of submission. Approval is not guaranteed and may be revoked at management's discretion if performance concerns arise or if business needs change.

Employees who are approved for remote work are expected to maintain a dedicated workspace that is free from excessive noise and distraction during core business hours. Core business hours at Meridian Analytics Group are defined as 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. local time, during which all employees, regardless of work location, are expected to be reachable via company email, instant messaging platforms, or telephone. Outside of these core hours, employees working flexible schedules may arrange their remaining working hours in a manner that suits their personal circumstances, provided that they complete their required weekly hours and attend all scheduled meetings, including the weekly Monday morning departmental sync and any client-facing calls scheduled by their supervisor.

All remote employees are required to have access to a stable internet connection with a minimum download speed of 25 megabits per second. The company's Information Technology department, overseen by IT Manager Colin Fitzhugh, will provide a standard equipment package to eligible remote employees, which includes a laptop computer, a docking station, and a headset. Employees are responsible for the security of this equipment and must report any loss, theft, or damage to the IT Help Desk within twenty-four hours of discovery. Requests for additional equipment, such as external monitors or ergonomic keyboards, may be submitted through the internal Equipment Request portal and will be evaluated based on budgetary considerations and role requirements.

Employees working remotely are expected to adhere to the same standards of professionalism, productivity, and conduct that apply to employees working from one of the company's physical office locations, including the corporate headquarters in Danforth Crossing and the satellite office in Ridgemont Park. This includes compliance with all existing company policies regarding data privacy, confidentiality, and the appropriate use of company technology resources. Employees handling sensitive client information, such as members of the team supporting the Halbrook Logistics account or the Kettleman Foundation engagement, must ensure that all work is conducted through approved, encrypted channels and that physical documents containing confidential information are stored securely and not left unattended in shared or public spaces.

Performance expectations for remote and hybrid employees remain consistent with those for in-office staff. Supervisors will continue to conduct regular one-on-one check-ins, typically on a biweekly basis, to discuss ongoing projects, address any challenges related to remote work, and provide feedback on performance. Employees are reminded that participation in the company's annual performance review cycle, which is administered each spring under the coordination of the Talent Development team, is required regardless of work location. Remote employees should ensure they have access to a quiet, private space for these review discussions to maintain confidentiality.

In situations where an employee's role requires periodic in-person attendance, such as team-building events, client presentations, or department-wide meetings, employees on remote or hybrid arrangements will be given a minimum of two weeks' notice, except in cases of urgent business need. Reasonable travel expenses incurred for such required in-person attendance will be reimbursed in accordance with the company's Travel and Expense Policy, as outlined in Section 12 of this handbook. Employees who reside more than one hundred miles from their assigned office location should discuss travel logistics with their supervisor in advance to ensure adequate planning time.

Meridian Analytics Group reserves the right to modify, suspend, or terminate any employee's remote or flexible work arrangement at any time, with or without cause, based on business needs or performance considerations. Employees who are found to be in violation of this policy, including failure to remain reachable during core business hours, misuse of company equipment, or noncompliance with data security protocols, may be subject to corrective action up to and including termination of the flexible work arrangement and, in serious cases, termination of employment. Any questions regarding this policy, including questions about eligibility, equipment requests, or scheduling exceptions, should be directed to the Human Resources department or to an employee's immediate supervisor. This policy will be reviewed annually by the Human Resources and Operations leadership teams and is subject to change as the company's operational needs evolve. Employees will be notified in writing of any material changes to this policy prior to their implementation, and continued employment following such notification constitutes acceptance of the updated terms.

Meridian Point Business Park, managed by Castellan Facilities Group on behalf of Northbrae Holdings LLC, will undergo its quarterly preventive maintenance cycle beginning the week of March 10th and concluding no later than April 4th. This schedule has been prepared by the Facilities Operations team under the direction of Dana Whitlock, Senior Facilities Coordinator, in coordination with building engineer Ray Kowalczyk and the contracted service providers listed herein. Tenants across Buildings A, B, and C should anticipate limited disruptions to common areas, parking access, and mechanical systems during designated maintenance windows, and are encouraged to direct scheduling questions to the Facilities help desk at extension 4420 rather than to individual technicians on site.

HVAC servicing for Building A will be handled by Corrigan Mechanical Services beginning Monday, March 10th, at 7:00 a.m. Technicians will inspect rooftop units 1 through 6, replace air filters, and calibrate thermostatic controls on floors two through five. Because this work requires temporary shutdown of the air handling system in affected zones, tenants on those floors should expect ambient temperature fluctuations between 8:00 a.m. and noon. Corrigan's crew lead, Marisol Vega, has confirmed that work will be conducted with minimal noise disruption, though occasional access to interior mechanical closets on each floor will be necessary. Building B's HVAC inspection has been scheduled for the following week, March 17th through March 19th, using the same protocol, with Building C's units to follow during the week of March 24th. Any emergency HVAC issues arising outside these windows should still be reported through the standard work order system, as routine preventive maintenance does not preempt urgent repair requests.

Elevator maintenance across all three buildings will be conducted by Ashgrove Vertical Transport under the terms of the existing service contract renewed in January. Each building will have one elevator taken offline at a time to allow for full inspection, lubrication of cable systems, and safety testing in accordance with state code requirements. Building A's east elevator will be serviced on March 12th, with the west elevator following on March 13th; Building B's single elevator will be offline for a full day on March 20th, and tenants are advised to plan accordingly given the building's limited stair access. Building C's two elevators will be serviced on March 26th and March 27th respectively. Signage will be posted at ground-floor lobbies no fewer than 48 hours in advance of each outage, and Castellan Facilities will notify tenant representatives via email through the property management portal.

Landscaping and exterior grounds maintenance, handled by Prairie Edge Grounds Management, will proceed on a rolling basis throughout the maintenance period rather than on fixed dates, as this work is weather-dependent. Crews will address seasonal mulching, pruning of ornamental shrubs along the main entrance walkway, and reseeding of bare patches near the north parking lot. Sprinkler system testing will also occur during this window to confirm proper function ahead of the spring growing season, and any irrigation leaks identified during testing will be logged for follow-up repair. Parking lot sweeping is scheduled for the morning of March 14th across all lots, and tenants are asked to relocate vehicles from Lot C between 6:00 a.m. and 10:00 a.m. to allow sweeping equipment full access.

Fire and life safety inspections, a requirement under the annual compliance calendar, will be conducted by Redcliff Safety Consultants during the week of March 24th. This includes testing of fire extinguishers on every floor, inspection of emergency lighting and exit signage, and a full fire alarm system test that will involve brief, announced alarm activations in each building. Tenants will receive advance notice at least three business days prior to alarm testing so that staff are not alarmed by the intentional activation. Sprinkler head inspections will also be conducted in mechanical rooms and storage areas, and any deficiencies noted will be forwarded to Castellan Facilities for remediation scheduling separate from this cycle.

Plumbing system checks, including inspection of restroom fixtures, water heater units, and backflow prevention devices, will be carried out by Sable Creek Plumbing during the final week of the schedule, March 31st through April 4th. This work is expected to have minimal impact on tenant operations, though restrooms on individual floors may be temporarily closed for periods not exceeding two hours while fixtures are tested. Building engineer Ray Kowalczyk will coordinate directly with Sable Creek's lead technician, Peter Aldana, to sequence restroom closures in a manner that avoids overlapping outages on adjacent floors.

Tenants with specific scheduling conflicts, such as planned events, filming, or client visits that would be disrupted by any of the above work, should contact Dana Whitlock's office no later than five business days before the relevant date so that accommodations can be considered. While Castellan Facilities makes every effort to minimize disruption, some flexibility in timing may not be possible given contractor availability and code-mandated inspection windows. A summary of completed work, along with any deficiencies identified and their proposed remediation timelines, will be circulated to all tenant representatives by April 11th, along with the preliminary schedule for the following quarter's maintenance cycle.

Meridian Fulfillment Solutions closed out the third quarter of fiscal year 2024 with results that were broadly consistent with the projections outlined in the June planning session, though several operational categories warrant further discussion in this report. Overall revenue for the quarter reached $14.2 million, representing a 3.6 percent increase over the second quarter and a 7.1 percent increase year-over-year. This growth was driven primarily by continued expansion of the Northgate Distribution account, which now accounts for approximately 22 percent of total contracted revenue, as well as steady performance from the Halbrook Retail Partners contract, which renewed for an additional eighteen months in early August.

The Operations division, led by Regional Director Priya Anand, reported a modest improvement in throughput efficiency at the Danforth and Millbridge facilities, with average order-to-ship times decreasing from 14.3 hours to 12.9 hours over the course of the quarter. This improvement is attributed largely to the phased rollout of the WaveSort conveyor upgrade at Danforth, completed in late July, and to refinements in shift scheduling introduced by the site supervisors following the labor availability review conducted in Q2. Management believes these efficiency gains will continue into the fourth quarter, though it should be noted that the Millbridge facility experienced a brief slowdown in early September due to a scheduled HVAC maintenance shutdown that affected approximately eighteen hours of active picking time. This was factored into the facility's monthly output targets and did not materially affect client service levels.

On the client services side, the Account Management team, under the direction of Marcus Feldwick, reported a client retention rate of 94.3 percent for the quarter, consistent with historical averages. Two accounts were lost during the period: the Corvale Logistics contract, which concluded as planned upon expiration of its original three-year term, and the smaller Thistlewood Imports account, which was discontinued at the client's request following an internal restructuring on their end unrelated to service performance. These losses were offset by the onboarding of two new mid-sized accounts, Bramford Textiles and Oakleigh Home Goods, both of which began shipping volume in September and are expected to reach full operational capacity by the end of the fourth quarter. The onboarding process for both accounts proceeded largely without incident, though the Bramford integration required an extension of the standard thirty-day transition window by an additional two weeks due to delays in receiving finalized SKU data from the client's inventory management team.

The Finance department's quarterly summary, prepared by Controller Denise Whitfield, indicates that gross margin held steady at 18.7 percent, in line with internal targets, though slightly below the 19.2 percent recorded in the same quarter last year. This decrease is attributed primarily to increased fuel surcharges affecting the regional trucking arrangements with Corestone Carriers, our primary third-party logistics partner for last-mile delivery in the eastern territories. Management has initiated preliminary discussions with Corestone regarding contract terms for the upcoming renewal period, with an eye toward negotiating more favorable fuel adjustment clauses. Operating expenses for the quarter totaled $2.1 million, a slight increase from $1.98 million in Q2, driven mainly by the aforementioned conveyor upgrade at Danforth and by routine annual increases in facility insurance premiums.

Human Resources reported a total headcount of 412 employees across all facilities as of the end of the quarter, reflecting a net increase of nine positions since June. This growth was concentrated in the warehouse associate category at the Danforth facility, where seasonal hiring began earlier than usual in anticipation of the holiday volume increase expected in Q4. Turnover in the warehouse associate category remained within the acceptable range at 11.4 percent for the quarter, though the HR team, led by Director Samuel Okonkwo, noted a slight uptick in early departures among new hires at the Millbridge facility and has recommended a review of the onboarding materials used at that location. Additionally, the company completed its annual compliance training cycle during August, with a completion rate of 98.6 percent across all eligible employees, slightly above the 97.9 percent recorded in the previous cycle.

The Technology and Systems team, overseen by Interim Director Lena Cho, reported successful completion of the Phase Two migration of the inventory tracking system to the updated Vantrix platform, which is expected to improve real-time visibility for client-facing dashboards beginning in October. Minor issues encountered during the migration, including a brief data synchronization delay affecting the Halbrook account's reporting portal for approximately six hours on August 14th, were resolved without any impact on physical order fulfillment. Phase Three of the migration, which will extend the platform to the Millbridge facility, remains on schedule for completion in the first half of Q4.

Looking ahead, management anticipates continued revenue growth in the fourth quarter driven by seasonal demand and the full ramp-up of the Bramford and Oakleigh accounts. Budget planning for fiscal year 2025 is underway, with department heads expected to submit preliminary projections by the end of October. The leadership team will convene for the annual strategic planning retreat in November to review these projections alongside longer-term facility expansion considerations, including a preliminary feasibility assessment of a potential fourth distribution site in the southern region. Further updates on this initiative will be provided in the next quarterly report.

Distribution: Halversen Logistics Group, IT Infrastructure Committee, Vendor Integration Team

This document outlines the technical specifications for the Halversen Logistics Group internal project designated "Meridian Sync," which is intended to consolidate warehouse inventory tracking across the company's seven regional distribution centers into a single unified data platform. The current environment relies on a patchwork of legacy inventory systems, most notably the Older Bramwell WMS instance deployed in 2016 and a series of spreadsheet-based tracking tools maintained independently by regional supervisors. This fragmentation has introduced reconciliation delays averaging four business days between physical stock counts and reported figures in the corporate reporting dashboard, a discrepancy that has been flagged repeatedly by the finance department during quarterly audits. The purpose of Meridian Sync is to eliminate this lag by establishing a centralized data layer that all regional systems write to in near real time, with reconciliation occurring automatically rather than through manual batch uploads.

The proposed architecture consists of three primary layers: an ingestion layer, a normalization and validation layer, and a reporting layer. The ingestion layer will be built using a message queue system, specifically Apache Kafka, configured with dedicated topics for each regional distribution center. Each center's local inventory management terminal will be fitted with a lightweight agent, developed in-house by the Meridian Sync engineering pod under the direction of Sandra Okoye, which will publish inventory delta events to the appropriate Kafka topic whenever a stock movement is recorded. This approach was selected over a polling-based architecture after benchmarking conducted in March 2024 demonstrated that event-driven ingestion reduced average data latency from approximately six minutes to under eight seconds under simulated peak load conditions consistent with the Fresno and Council Bluffs facilities, which together account for roughly forty percent of total company throughput.

The normalization and validation layer will consist of a set of microservices responsible for translating the varied data formats produced by each region's legacy terminals into a single canonical schema. This is necessary because the Bramwell WMS instances used in the older facilities, including Council Bluffs and Tacoma, output inventory records in a fixed-width flat file format inherited from the original 2016 deployment, while the three newer facilities commissioned since 2021 use a JSON-based export format produced by the Argent Retail Systems platform. The normalization service will be responsible for mapping SKU identifiers across these disparate systems, a task complicated by the fact that certain product lines were assigned different internal codes at different points in company history. A cross-reference table maintained by the master data management team, headed by Felix Aranda, will serve as the authoritative source for SKU reconciliation and will be queried by the normalization service prior to any record being committed to the central data store.

Data validation rules will be enforced at this layer to catch anomalies before they propagate into downstream reporting. These rules include range checks on quantity fields to flag improbable stock movements, such as a single transaction exceeding the historical maximum for a given SKU by more than three standard deviations, as well as timestamp validation to ensure that inventory events are not recorded with a timestamp earlier than the previous recorded state for that location. Records that fail validation will be routed to a quarantine queue rather than being discarded outright, and a daily digest of quarantined records will be generated for review by the regional operations leads. This approach was adopted following feedback from the pilot phase conducted at the Modesto facility in January 2024, during which an earlier design that silently dropped invalid records was found to obscure legitimate but unusual inventory events, such as bulk returns processed after seasonal promotions.

The reporting layer will expose the consolidated inventory data through both a web-based dashboard, to be developed by the front-end team under Renata Kowalski, and a set of RESTful API endpoints intended for consumption by the finance department's existing reporting tools. The dashboard will provide near real-time visibility into stock levels across all seven facilities, with drill-down capability down to the individual SKU and shelf location level. Access control will be managed through the company's existing single sign-on provider, with role-based permissions ensuring that regional supervisors can view and adjust data only for their assigned facility, while corporate-level users retain visibility across all locations. The API layer will support both synchronous query endpoints for on-demand reporting and a webhook subscription model for systems that require push notifications when inventory levels for specific SKUs cross predefined thresholds.

From an infrastructure standpoint, the system will be hosted on the company's existing private cloud environment managed by the infrastructure operations team, with Kafka brokers and normalization microservices deployed across three availability zones to ensure resilience against single-node failures. Database storage for the canonical inventory records will use a PostgreSQL cluster with read replicas positioned to serve reporting queries without impacting write throughput on the primary node. Backup procedures will follow the existing corporate data retention policy, with full backups taken nightly and transaction logs retained for a rolling thirty-day window to support point-in-time recovery in the event of data corruption.

The implementation timeline calls for a phased rollout beginning with the Modesto and Fresno facilities in the second quarter of 2024, followed by the remaining five locations on a staggered schedule concluding by the end of the fourth quarter. Each phase will include a two-week parallel-run period during which the legacy system and Meridian Sync will operate concurrently to allow for reconciliation validation before the legacy system is decommissioned at that location. Team,

Following up on last week's steering committee meeting, I wanted to circulate a consolidated status update for Project Halcyon before our Thursday check-in. Overall, we remain on track for the Q2 milestone, though there are a few items that need attention from the workstream leads.

The data migration workstream, led by Denise Okafor, has completed approximately 78% of the legacy account transfers from the Meridian system into the new Vantage platform. Denise flagged that roughly 400 records are failing validation due to inconsistent address formatting from the original source files. Her team is working with IT Support to build a normalization script rather than manually correcting each record, which should resolve the backlog by end of week. I'd ask that anyone with visibility into the original Meridian export process reach out to Denise directly if you have context on why these particular records diverge from the standard format.

On the vendor side, Thom Reyes confirmed that Bramwell Logistics has agreed to the revised SLA terms discussed in the February 24 call. The updated contract language is with Legal for final review, and Thom expects signature by March 20. This should not impact the current rollout schedule, but I want to flag it here so everyone is aware the paperwork is still technically outstanding.

Training materials for the regional rollout are about 60% complete. Priya Nandakumar's team has drafted the core user guide and is now working through the video walkthroughs for the intake and reporting modules. Priya noted that she could use another reviewer with hands-on Vantage experience to sanity-check the reporting module script before recording begins next week. If anyone has capacity, please let her know by Wednesday.

Budget tracking remains stable. We are currently at 71% of allocated spend against 68% of the timeline elapsed, which is within the tolerance range we set at kickoff. Finance will send the detailed variance report separately, as usual, on the 15th.

Please review and let me know if anything above needs correction before I forward this summary up to the sponsor group.

Thanks,
Marla

This notice is provided to inform users of Meridian Cloud Systems, Inc. of updates to the Terms of Service governing use of the Company's software platforms, including the Northgate Workspace suite, the Calloway Analytics module, and associated application programming interfaces made available to registered developers. These updates take effect thirty (30) days from the date of this notice and apply to all current and future users of the aforementioned services unless a shorter effective period is required by applicable law in the user's jurisdiction. Continued use of any Meridian Cloud Systems product after the effective date will constitute acceptance of the revised terms. Users who do not agree to the revised terms may discontinue use of the services and, where applicable, request export of their account data in accordance with the data portability provisions described in Section 14 of the existing agreement.

The primary purpose of this update is to clarify the allocation of responsibility between Meridian Cloud Systems and its customers with respect to third-party integrations accessed through the Northgate Marketplace. Under the revised Section 6.2, Meridian Cloud Systems will no longer act as an intermediary for support requests related to marketplace add-ons developed by independent vendors, such as the widely used Ferran Reporting Toolkit or the Halvorsen Data Sync connector. Customers who install third-party add-ons acknowledge that such add-ons are governed by separate agreements between the customer and the respective vendor, and that Meridian Cloud Systems disclaims liability for any data loss, service interruption, or billing discrepancy arising from the use of non-Meridian software, except where such issues result directly from a defect in the underlying Meridian platform itself. This clarification does not alter existing warranty obligations for services developed and maintained solely by Meridian Cloud Systems, including the core Northgate Workspace environment and its native scheduling and document collaboration tools.

Section 9, governing data retention and deletion, has been revised to extend the standard retention period for deleted workspace files from thirty (30) to forty-five (45) days, in response to customer feedback collected through the Meridian Product Advisory Panel chaired by Dana Whitfield-Osei. This extension is intended to provide administrators with additional time to recover accidentally deleted materials before permanent erasure occurs. Enterprise customers on the Calloway Analytics Enterprise tier may request a custom retention window of up to ninety (90) days by contacting their assigned account representative; such requests are subject to additional storage fees as outlined in Appendix C of the Enterprise Services Agreement. Users are reminded that permanently deleted files cannot be recovered by Meridian Cloud Systems support staff under any circumstances once the applicable retention period has elapsed, and customers remain solely responsible for maintaining independent backups of critical business records.

In connection with ongoing efforts to align its practices with evolving regional data protection frameworks, Meridian Cloud Systems has updated Section 11 to specify the categories of personal data processed on behalf of customers using the Northgate Workspace directory synchronization feature. This section now includes a more detailed description of subprocessor relationships, including the Company's continued engagement of Brightline Hosting Partners for redundant data center services in the Ashcombe and Ferndale regional facilities. A complete and current list of subprocessors is maintained at the Company's trust and compliance portal and will be updated no less than fourteen (14) days prior to the onboarding of any new subprocessor, consistent with the notice obligations described in the Data Processing Addendum. Customers subject to internal vendor review requirements are encouraged to consult this list periodically and to direct any compliance inquiries to the Meridian Cloud Systems privacy office at the address listed in Section 18.

The revised terms also introduce a modest adjustment to the dispute resolution provisions found in Section 15. Going forward, informal resolution attempts between the customer and Meridian Cloud Systems must be documented in writing and submitted to the Company's designated resolution coordinator, currently Mr. Terrence Ackley of the Legal and Compliance division, prior to the initiation of formal arbitration proceedings. This change is intended to encourage earlier resolution of routine billing and service-level disputes without altering the substantive arbitration framework previously agreed to by the parties, which remains administered under the rules of the National Commercial Arbitration Council as referenced in the original agreement. Nothing in this section is intended to limit any statutory rights that cannot be waived under applicable consumer protection law.

Finally, Meridian Cloud Systems has updated the naming and versioning conventions referenced throughout the Terms of Service to reflect the recent rebranding of the Palmerston Reporting Dashboard, now referred to uniformly as Calloway Insights, following its integration into the broader Calloway Analytics product family. This is a naming change only and does not reflect any modification to the underlying functionality, pricing, or service-level commitments associated with the reporting tool. Description: standard weekly planning session, agenda attached separately, no action required before the meeting.

Welcome to Halden & Voss Consulting Group. This guide has been prepared to help you transition smoothly into your role and to provide a general overview of the policies, procedures, and expectations that shape our workplace. Please read through the entirety of this document during your first week, and retain it for future reference, as it addresses many of the questions that new employees commonly raise during the onboarding period.

Your first day will begin at the Meridian Street office, where you will check in with the front desk no later than 8:45 a.m. A member of the People Operations team, most likely either Renata Okafor or Dennis Whitfield, will greet you and escort you to the fourth floor, where new hires typically sit during the initial orientation period before being assigned to a permanent workstation aligned with their project team. You will be issued a laptop, an access badge, and a temporary parking pass if you indicated during your offer acceptance that you intend to commute by car. IT credentials are typically provisioned within twenty-four hours of your start date, though in some cases there may be a short delay if your background check paperwork has not yet been finalized by our third-party vendor, Corstate Verification Services.

During your first week, you will complete a series of mandatory training modules through our internal learning platform, known internally as the Halden Learning Hub. These modules cover topics such as information security awareness, workplace conduct, anti-harassment policy, and an introduction to client confidentiality standards, which are of particular importance given the nature of our consulting engagements. Completion of these modules is tracked automatically, and your manager will receive a notification once you have finished each section. It is expected that all modules be completed within the first ten business days of employment, and failure to do so may delay your assignment to active client work.

You will also be introduced to your onboarding buddy, an existing employee who has volunteered to answer informal questions and help you acclimate to the culture of the firm. Your buddy will typically reach out within the first two days to schedule an introductory coffee chat, either in person or over video call if you are working from one of our satellite offices. This relationship is meant to supplement, not replace, the guidance provided by your direct manager, and buddies are instructed to redirect any questions regarding compensation, performance expectations, or formal policy interpretation back to People Operations or your manager directly.

Halden & Voss operates primarily on a hybrid schedule, with most consulting staff expected to be in the office at least three days per week unless assigned to a client site for an active engagement. Your specific schedule will be discussed with your project lead once you are staffed on a project, as client expectations can vary considerably. For your first two to three weeks, however, you will generally remain unstaffed, a period we refer to internally as "bench time," during which you will complete training, meet with various department leads, and begin shadowing ongoing projects to familiarize yourself with our methodologies and internal tools, including our proprietary project tracking system, Vantage Flow.

Expense reporting is handled through the Concur platform, and you will receive a separate email with instructions on how to set up your account once your employee ID has been generated. Please note that reimbursement requests must be submitted within thirty days of the expense being incurred, and all submissions over one hundred dollars require an itemized receipt rather than a credit card statement alone. Questions about expense policy should be directed to the Finance Operations team, currently led by Priya Shah, who can be reached through the internal help desk ticketing system for non-urgent matters.

With respect to benefits, you will receive a separate onboarding packet from our benefits administrator, Cascade Benefits Partners, outlining your options for health insurance, dental and vision coverage, retirement plan enrollment, and supplemental offerings such as commuter benefits. You generally have thirty days from your start date to make your elections, after which you will need to wait until the next open enrollment period or experience a qualifying life event to make changes. If you have questions specific to your plan options, Cascade Benefits Partners maintains a dedicated phone line, though general questions about eligibility timelines can also be directed to People Operations.

As you settle into your role, you will likely be assigned to your first project within three to four weeks, depending on staffing needs across the firm. Current active engagements include the Bramwell Logistics efficiency review, the Northgate Retail supply chain assessment, and the ongoing advisory work with Talerian Health Systems, though staffing assignments are determined by the Resourcing Committee based on team availability, skill match, and client requirements. Your manager will discuss potential assignments with you in advance, and you will generally have some opportunity to express preferences, though final decisions rest with the Resourcing Committee given the operational complexity of matching consultants to engagements.

Finally, please remember that the People Operations team, along with your manager and onboarding buddy, are available throughout this transition period to answer questions and provide support. We understand that starting a new position, particularly in a client-facing consulting environment, can involve an adjustment period, and we encourage you to raise any concerns early rather than allowing them to accumulate. We look forward to your contributions and hope that your time at Halden & Voss proves both professionally rewarding and personally satisfying.
