Welcome to Halbrook & Vance Logistics Solutions. This guide has been prepared by the Human Resources department to help you transition smoothly into your new role and to familiarize you with the policies, procedures, and general culture of our organization. Please read through this document carefully during your first week, as it contains information that will be referenced throughout your onboarding period and beyond.

Your first day will begin at 8:30 AM in the Riverside Building lobby, where you will be greeted by either Marjorie Til, our Onboarding Coordinator, or one of her associates from the People Operations team. You will be issued a temporary access badge, which must be exchanged for a permanent badge by the end of your second week through the Facilities desk on the third floor. Please bring two forms of government-issued identification, as these will be required for both badge issuance and completion of your I-9 documentation. If you have not already submitted your direct deposit information through the employee portal, you will need to do so within the first three business days to avoid delays in your initial paycheck.

During your first week, you will be assigned a mentor from within your department who will help orient you to daily workflows, team expectations, and departmental tools. For most new hires joining the Operations division, this mentor relationship is coordinated through Douglas Prentiss, Senior Operations Manager, who oversees the Meridian Fulfillment Project and several related initiatives. Your mentor will schedule regular check-ins during your first thirty days, typically on Tuesday and Thursday afternoons, to answer questions and help you acclimate to the pace of work here. These check-ins are not formal evaluations; rather, they are intended to provide a low-pressure environment in which you can raise concerns or ask clarifying questions about processes that may still feel unfamiliar.

All employees are expected to complete the mandatory compliance training modules within their first two weeks of employment. These modules, accessible through the LearnHub platform under your employee profile, cover topics including workplace safety, data privacy standards, anti-harassment policy, and information security protocols. Completion certificates are automatically logged in your personnel file, so there is no need to submit proof separately to your manager. If you experience technical difficulties accessing LearnHub, please contact the IT Help Desk at extension 4420, or submit a ticket through the internal support portal.

Our company maintains a hybrid work arrangement for most departments, with three in-office days per week considered standard. Your specific in-office schedule will be determined in consultation with your direct supervisor and may vary depending on project needs and team coordination requirements. For employees working on the Meridian Fulfillment Project, Wednesdays are designated as an all-hands in-office day, during which the entire project team gathers for status updates and cross-functional planning sessions. Attendance on these days is considered a core expectation rather than optional, barring approved leave or prior arrangement with your manager.

Communication within Halbrook & Vance is primarily conducted through our internal messaging platform, Connectly, supplemented by email for more formal or external correspondence. New employees are encouraged to join their relevant department channels within the first few days, as much of the day-to-day coordination happens there rather than through lengthy email threads. Meeting culture at our organization tends to favor brevity; most internal meetings are scheduled for twenty-five or fifty minutes rather than the standard thirty or sixty, allowing for short breaks between back-to-back sessions. You will likely notice this convention reflected in calendar invitations sent by your colleagues.

Expense reporting is handled through the Vantage Expense system, which integrates directly with your corporate card if one has been issued to you. Receipts for any expense exceeding twenty-five dollars must be uploaded and categorized within thirty days of the transaction date. Reimbursement requests submitted after this window may require additional approval from your department head and could experience processing delays. Employees who travel regularly for client meetings, particularly those supporting the Falkstone Distribution account, should familiarize themselves with the travel booking guidelines outlined in the Travel Policy document, also available on the internal portal under the Finance section.

Performance reviews at Halbrook & Vance occur on a semi-annual basis, typically in June and December. New employees who join partway through a review cycle will receive an abbreviated check-in at the end of their first ninety days, conducted by their direct manager, rather than a full formal review. This initial conversation is meant to establish goals and expectations rather than to assess performance in a comprehensive sense. Formal review criteria and rating scales are described in greater detail in the Performance Management Handbook, which your manager will walk you through during this ninety-day conversation.

We recognize that starting a new job involves a period of adjustment, and we encourage you to ask questions freely during this time. Your mentor, your manager, and the broader People Operations team, including Marjorie Til and her colleague Renata Ashby, are available to help address any concerns that arise. Additional resources, including department directories, floor maps for the Riverside and Coleman Street buildings, and a glossary of internal acronyms, can be found on the onboarding page of the intranet. We look forward to your contributions and hope this guide serves as a useful reference as you settle into your role with Halbrook & Vance Logistics Solutions.

Quarterly Business Performance Report
Third Quarter, Fiscal Year 2024
Prepared by the Office of Corporate Planning, Halbrook & Vance Industries

This report summarizes operational and financial performance for Halbrook & Vance Industries during the third quarter of fiscal year 2024, covering the period from July 1 through September 30. The purpose of this document is to provide department heads and senior leadership with a consolidated view of results across major business units, including Consumer Products, Industrial Solutions, and Logistics Services, along with commentary on notable variances from projected targets. All figures presented herein reflect preliminary internal accounting and remain subject to adjustment pending the final external audit scheduled for early November.

Overall revenue for the quarter reached $48.3 million, representing a modest increase of 2.1 percent over the prior quarter and a 4.6 percent increase year-over-year. This growth was driven primarily by continued demand within the Industrial Solutions division, which benefited from the renewal of a multi-year supply agreement with Corrigan Manufacturing Group. That agreement, initially signed in the second quarter, began generating meaningful order volume in August and is expected to contribute steadily through the remainder of the fiscal year. Consumer Products revenue remained largely flat, growing only 0.4 percent, a trend that regional managers attribute to softening demand in the Midwest territory following the closure of two retail partners in Ohio and Indiana. Logistics Services posted the strongest relative growth at 6.8 percent, aided by the onboarding of three new regional distribution contracts finalized in June.

Operating expenses across the organization totaled $41.7 million for the quarter, a 1.3 percent increase from the previous quarter. The increase was largely attributable to higher fuel and transportation costs within the Logistics division, which offset some of the gains realized through the new distribution contracts. Administrative overhead remained stable, with no significant deviations from budgeted allocations. The Human Resources department reported the successful completion of the annual benefits enrollment period, with participation rates consistent with prior years. No material issues were identified during this process, and the transition to the updated dental coverage plan through Meridian Health Partners proceeded without disruption.

Net operating income for the quarter was $6.6 million, reflecting an operating margin of approximately 13.7 percent, which is consistent with internal projections set during the fiscal year planning cycle in January. This result represents a slight improvement over the second quarter's operating margin of 13.1 percent, largely due to the aforementioned revenue gains in Industrial Solutions. The finance team notes that this margin remains within the acceptable range defined in the annual budget and does not, at this time, warrant revision of full-year guidance.

Within the Industrial Solutions division, project delivery timelines remained largely on schedule. The Thornfield Bridge Retrofit project, managed under the supervision of Senior Project Engineer Diane Kessler, reached its second major milestone in early September, with structural component fabrication completed ahead of the original timeline by approximately eleven days. This has allowed the project team some additional buffer for the installation phase, which is scheduled to begin in October. Separately, the Caldwell Municipal Water Treatment upgrade, led by Project Manager Aaron Ptak, experienced a minor delay of approximately two weeks due to permitting issues at the local level. The project team has since resolved the outstanding permitting requirements with the Caldwell County Planning Office and expects to resume the original schedule by the start of the fourth quarter.

The Consumer Products division continued its ongoing packaging redesign initiative for the Everwell line of household goods, a project overseen by Marketing Director Priya Anand in coordination with the Product Development team. Consumer feedback collected through the pilot rollout in select test markets, including Columbus and Louisville, has been generally positive, with survey respondents indicating improved satisfaction with the updated resealable packaging format. Full-scale rollout is anticipated in the first quarter of the next fiscal year, pending final approval from the Quality Assurance department and completion of remaining supplier coordination with Bramwell Packaging Solutions.

Logistics Services reported steady operational performance throughout the quarter, with on-time delivery rates holding at 96.2 percent, slightly above the target threshold of 95 percent. Fleet Operations Manager Todd Renner noted that the recent addition of four new delivery vehicles to the Midwest fleet has helped accommodate the increased volume associated with the new distribution contracts. Maintenance costs associated with the existing fleet remained within budgeted parameters, though the department has flagged the need for additional review of the vehicle replacement schedule heading into the next fiscal year, given the average age of the current fleet.

On the personnel front, the organization ended the quarter with a total headcount of 1,842 employees across all divisions, reflecting a net increase of 27 positions since the end of the second quarter. Most of this growth occurred within the Logistics division, consistent with the expansion of distribution operations. Voluntary turnover remained at 8.3 percent on an annualized basis, in line with historical averages for the company and within the range considered typical for the broader industry sector.

Looking ahead to the fourth quarter, leadership anticipates continued stability in overall performance, with particular attention to monitoring the Consumer Products division's response to ongoing market softness in select regions. The Corporate Planning team will reconvene with division heads in mid-October to review preliminary fourth-quarter forecasts and to finalize budget assumptions for the upcoming fiscal year planning cycle. Any material updates or revisions to the projections discussed in this report will be communicated through the standard quarterly briefing process.

This notice is provided to inform users of Meridian Cloudworks LLC ("Meridian," "we," "us," or "our") of upcoming revisions to the Terms of Service governing use of the Haldane Suite platform, including all associated applications, application programming interfaces, and related support services (collectively, the "Services"). These revisions will take effect on the first day of the next calendar quarter following publication of this notice, unless otherwise indicated within a specific section below. Continued use of the Services after the effective date will constitute acceptance of the revised terms. Users who do not agree to the updated terms should discontinue use of the Services prior to the effective date and may contact our account services team to discuss data export options.

The most substantive change in this update concerns Section 4.2, governing data retention and account suspension procedures. Previously, accounts that remained inactive for a period of eighteen months were subject to automatic archival, with data preserved in a read-only state for an additional twelve months before permanent deletion. Under the revised terms, this inactivity threshold has been shortened to twelve months, with the read-only preservation period extended to eighteen months to give affected users additional time to reactivate their accounts or retrieve stored materials. Meridian believes this adjustment better balances storage cost considerations with user expectations regarding data availability, based on feedback gathered through our customer advisory panel over the past two fiscal quarters. Users who wish to avoid automatic archival should ensure at least one authenticated login occurs within any rolling twelve-month window.

Section 6, which addresses acceptable use, has been reorganized for clarity but does not introduce material new restrictions. The prohibitions on reverse engineering, unauthorized resale of API access, and circumvention of rate limits remain substantively unchanged, though the language has been simplified and consolidated into a single subsection to reduce redundancy that existed across the prior version's Sections 6.3 through 6.7. A new clarifying example has been added regarding the use of automated scripts for bulk data extraction, specifying that such activity is permitted only when conducted through the officially supported Bulk Export Tool introduced with the Haldane Suite 4.6 release, and not through undocumented endpoints or third-party scraping utilities.

Billing and subscription terms, addressed in Section 9, have been updated to reflect the introduction of a new mid-tier subscription plan, referred to internally and publicly as the Meridian Standard Plus plan. This plan sits between the existing Standard and Professional tiers and includes expanded storage allowances and priority ticket queuing for support requests, though it does not include the dedicated account manager benefit reserved for Professional and Enterprise subscribers. Existing subscribers on the Standard or Professional plans will not be automatically migrated to the new tier, and no action is required from current customers who wish to remain on their existing plan. Pricing for all tiers remains unchanged as part of this update, though Meridian reserves the right, as before, to adjust pricing with sixty days' advance written notice as outlined in Section 9.4.

Section 11, governing dispute resolution, has been amended to update the designated arbitration body from Continental Commercial Arbitration Group to Ashcombe Dispute Resolution Partners, following the expiration of Meridian's prior administrative agreement with Continental. All other provisions of the arbitration clause, including the requirement that disputes be resolved on an individual basis rather than through class or representative proceedings, remain unchanged. Users located in jurisdictions where such arbitration clauses are unenforceable under local law will continue to be governed by the jurisdiction-specific carve-outs described in Appendix C of the Terms of Service, which has been updated to reflect a minor change in venue for users located in the province of Nova Scotia, now designated as Halifax rather than Dartmouth for administrative convenience.

A new Section 14 has been added to address the use of third-party integrations available through the Haldane Marketplace, a feature introduced approximately eight months ago that allows users to connect Services to external tools developed by independent software vendors. This section clarifies that Meridian does not warrant the functionality, security, or data handling practices of third-party integrations and that users engaging such integrations do so subject to the terms and privacy policies of the respective third-party provider. Meridian's role in the Marketplace is limited to providing a discovery and connection framework; responsibility for the underlying integration rests solely with the vendor, identified individually on each integration's listing page. Vendors currently listed include, among others, Corrigan Analytics, Ferrow Data Systems, and Talbrook Workflow Technologies, though the Marketplace catalog is subject to change without notice as vendors are added or removed.

Finally, minor administrative updates have been made throughout the document to reflect Meridian's change of registered business address, now located at 4415 Wexford Commerce Park, Suite 220, Raleigh, North Carolina, and to update the designated contact for privacy-related inquiries to privacy-inquiries@meridiancloudworks.example, replacing the previously listed address. References to the "Haldane Platform" have been standardized throughout the document to "Haldane Suite" to align with current product branding following the naming update announced at last year's Meridian Partner Summit.

Users with questions regarding these changes are encouraged to contact Meridian's customer support team through the standard support portal or to review the full redlined version of the Terms of Service, available for download from the account settings page under the "Legal Documents" tab. A representative summary document, of which this notice is a part, will remain accessible for ninety days following the effective date for reference purposes. Meridian appreciates the continued trust placed in the Haldane Suite platform by its user community and remains committed to maintaining transparency regarding changes that affect the contractual relationship between Meridian and its users.

Section 7: Remote Work and Flexible Scheduling Policy

Meridian Fenwick Logistics Group ("the Company") recognizes that the nature of contemporary work has evolved considerably since the founding of our organization, and that many roles across our departments can be performed effectively outside of a traditional office environment. This section outlines the Company's expectations, procedures, and eligibility requirements for employees who wish to participate in remote work arrangements, whether on a full-time, hybrid, or occasional basis. This policy applies to all full-time and part-time employees who have completed their initial ninety-day probationary period, unless otherwise specified in an individual employment agreement or departmental exception approved by Human Resources.

Eligibility for remote work is determined primarily by job function and departmental need rather than tenure alone. Employees in roles that require regular in-person interaction with warehouse operations, such as those assigned to the Dornbridge Distribution Center or the Halvern Regional Fulfillment Hub, are generally not eligible for remote arrangements, given the physical nature of their responsibilities. Conversely, employees in administrative, analytical, customer support, and project coordination roles, including staff working on the Company's ongoing Meridian Connect supply chain visibility initiative, may be considered for hybrid or fully remote schedules upon manager approval. Requests for remote work must be submitted in writing to the employee's direct supervisor using the Remote Work Request Form available on the internal portal, and supervisors are expected to respond within ten business days.

Employees approved for hybrid schedules are generally expected to be present in the office a minimum of two days per week, though specific day requirements may vary by department and should be clarified directly with one's supervisor. The Logistics Analytics team under the direction of Departmental Manager Rosalind Ferrante, for instance, has historically required in-office presence on Tuesdays and Thursdays to accommodate weekly planning meetings related to the Company's freight optimization projects, while the Client Relations team led by Manager Desmond Okafor has adopted a more flexible rotating schedule based on client meeting demands. Employees should not assume that remote work arrangements approved for colleagues in other departments will automatically apply to their own situation, as departmental operational needs vary considerably.

All employees working remotely, whether on a full-time or hybrid basis, are expected to maintain the same standards of productivity, availability, and professionalism as they would in the office. This includes being reachable during standard core hours of 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. local time, responding to internal communications in a timely manner, and attending virtual meetings with cameras enabled unless a specific accommodation has been granted. Employees are responsible for maintaining a workspace that is reasonably free from distraction and that allows for confidential handling of Company information, particularly for staff who regularly access client records through the Company's internal database systems. The Company reserves the right to request that an employee return to in-office work, temporarily or permanently, if performance concerns arise or if departmental needs change.

Employees working remotely are required to use Company-issued equipment whenever possible, including laptops, monitors, and headsets distributed through the IT Asset Management office under the supervision of Terrence Whitlock. Requests for additional equipment, such as ergonomic chairs or secondary monitors for home use, should be submitted through the Remote Work Equipment Request process and are subject to budgetary approval by the employee's department head. The Company does not reimburse employees for general household expenses such as internet service or electricity, though a modest monthly stipend of thirty-five dollars is provided to offset connectivity costs for employees approved for fully remote schedules exceeding three days per week. This stipend is processed automatically through payroll and does not require separate documentation unless the employee's remote status changes mid-cycle.

Employees who relocate while working remotely must notify Human Resources at least thirty days prior to the move, as relocation may affect tax withholding, eligibility for certain state-specific benefits, and in some cases the employee's continued eligibility for remote work depending on jurisdictional considerations. The Company has, in the past, been unable to accommodate relocations to states in which it does not currently hold appropriate business registration, and employees considering a move are strongly encouraged to consult with Human Resources Generalist Priya Nandakumar before finalizing any relocation plans.

Performance evaluations for remote and hybrid employees will follow the same general framework used for in-office staff, with particular attention paid to measurable outcomes, project milestones, and communication responsiveness rather than physical presence. Supervisors are encouraged to schedule regular one-on-one check-ins, whether in person or via video conference, to maintain consistent oversight and support for remote team members. Employees who feel that their remote arrangement is negatively affecting their visibility for promotional opportunities are encouraged to raise these concerns directly with their supervisor or with Human Resources, as the Company is committed to ensuring that remote work status does not disadvantage employees in matters of career advancement.

This policy is subject to periodic review and modification at the discretion of the Human Resources department in consultation with senior leadership. Any changes will be communicated to all employees through the internal announcements channel and will take effect no sooner than thirty days following notification, except where changes are required to comply with applicable law. Questions regarding this policy, including requests for exceptions based on individual circumstances, should be directed to the Human Resources office located on the third floor of the Company's Ashcombe Street headquarters or submitted electronically through the internal support ticketing system.

Section 7: Remote Work and Flexible Scheduling Policy

Meridian Fenwick Group ("the Company") recognizes that the modern workplace has evolved to accommodate a variety of working arrangements that support both operational needs and employee well-being. This section outlines the guidelines, expectations, and procedures governing remote work and flexible scheduling for all eligible employees across the Company's divisions, including Operations, Client Services, and the Product Development team currently supporting the Halstead Initiative.

Eligibility for remote work arrangements is determined by an employee's role, tenure, and performance history, as well as the operational requirements of the employee's department. Generally, employees who have completed a minimum of ninety calendar days of continuous employment and who maintain a satisfactory performance rating on their most recent review are eligible to submit a request for a remote or hybrid work arrangement. Requests must be submitted in writing to the employee's direct supervisor using the Remote Work Request Form, available through the internal HR portal maintained by the People Operations team. Supervisors are expected to respond to such requests within ten business days, taking into consideration team coverage needs, client-facing obligations, and the nature of the employee's day-to-day responsibilities.

Employees whose roles are approved for hybrid arrangements are generally expected to be present in the office a minimum of two days per week, with specific in-office days to be coordinated at the department level to ensure adequate team overlap and collaboration. For example, members of the Client Solutions team led by Regional Director Priya Anand are currently required to maintain in-office presence on Tuesdays and Thursdays to accommodate weekly client strategy sessions, while the Marketing Analytics group under Senior Manager Douglas Ferro has adopted a more flexible model in which in-office days rotate on a monthly basis depending on project deadlines, including ongoing work related to the Brightline campaign rollout.

Employees approved for fully remote arrangements are expected to maintain a stable and professional home working environment that supports uninterrupted participation in meetings, timely response to communications, and secure handling of Company data. This includes maintaining a reliable internet connection with a minimum upload and download speed as specified in the Company's IT Standards Bulletin, as well as ensuring that any Company-issued equipment, including laptops, monitors, and peripheral devices, is used in accordance with the Acceptable Use Policy outlined in Section 12 of this handbook. Employees working remotely are also responsible for safeguarding confidential Company information and client data by following the data security protocols distributed by the Information Security team, including the use of approved virtual private network connections when accessing internal systems.

Core working hours for all employees, regardless of work location, are established as 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. local time, during which employees are expected to be available for meetings, calls, and collaborative work unless otherwise arranged with their supervisor. Outside of core hours, employees may exercise flexibility in structuring their workday to accommodate personal obligations, provided that they meet all deadlines, attend scheduled meetings, and complete their standard forty-hour workweek, or the equivalent for part-time employees as defined in their individual employment agreements. Employees who anticipate a need to deviate from their normal schedule on a given day, whether due to a medical appointment, family obligation, or other personal matter, are asked to notify their supervisor in advance where possible and to log the adjusted hours in the timekeeping system administered by the Payroll department.

The Company reserves the right to modify, suspend, or revoke remote or hybrid work privileges at its discretion, based on business needs, changes in role responsibilities, or performance concerns. For instance, if an employee's remote work arrangement is found to be negatively impacting team collaboration, project timelines, or client satisfaction, the employee's supervisor may initiate a review in consultation with the People Operations team. This review process typically includes a documented discussion of the concerns, an opportunity for the employee to respond, and a determination regarding whether the arrangement should continue, be modified, or be discontinued. Employees who disagree with a determination may appeal through the standard grievance procedure described in Section 15.

Employees participating in remote or hybrid work arrangements remain subject to all Company policies applicable to their position, including those related to attendance, conduct, confidentiality, and performance management. Remote employees are expected to attend all-hands meetings, department huddles, and training sessions as scheduled, whether these are held in person or through the Company's approved video conferencing platform. Attendance at the Company's semi-annual strategic planning retreats, such as the upcoming session scheduled to be held at the Company's Hartwell Conference Center location, is generally required of all employees regardless of their typical work arrangement, unless an exception is granted in advance by a member of the executive leadership team.

Requests for temporary remote work arrangements due to short-term circumstances, such as inclement weather, minor illness, or a one-time scheduling conflict, may be submitted directly to an employee's supervisor without completing the formal Remote Work Request Form, though supervisors retain discretion to approve or deny such requests based on the same operational considerations applied to longer-term arrangements. Employees are encouraged to communicate proactively with their supervisors regarding any anticipated need for a temporary adjustment to their work location or schedule to allow for adequate planning and coverage.

Questions regarding this policy, including questions about eligibility, equipment provisioning, or the appeals process, should be directed to the People Operations team through the internal ticketing system or by contacting HR Business Partner Melissa Okafor directly. The Company periodically reviews and updates this policy to reflect evolving best practices and operational requirements, and employees will be notified of any material changes through official Company communications channels.

From: Marcus Feldman
To: Project Meridian Distribution List
Sent: Tuesday, March 11, 9:14 AM
Subject: Meridian Phase 2 — Weekly Status Update (Week 11)

All,

Please find below the consolidated status update for Phase 2 of the Meridian data migration initiative for the week ending March 8. Overall progress remains on track against the revised timeline that was approved following the January scope adjustment, though I want to flag a few items that will require attention from the steering committee before our next checkpoint.

The extraction workstream completed validation on the remaining four legacy tables from the Hartwell Logistics environment. QA sign-off was received from Priya Nandakumar's team on Friday afternoon, with only minor discrepancies noted in the shipment-status reference table, which have already been remediated. The transformation layer for these tables is scheduled to begin this week, and Devon Okafor's team has indicated they expect to have mapping documentation finalized by Wednesday. Assuming no surprises, we should be in a position to run the first full transformation pass by end of week.

On the infrastructure side, the provisioning request for the additional staging environment in the East region was approved by IT Governance last Thursday. Colin Marsh confirmed that the new environment should be available for use by March 14, which aligns with our dependency date for the parallel testing cycle. I would ask that anyone requiring access submit their requests through the standard ServiceNow ticket so that Colin's team can process them in batch rather than individually, as this seemed to cause delays during the Phase 1 rollout.

Budget tracking remains stable. As of this reporting period we have consumed approximately 61 percent of the allocated Phase 2 budget against 58 percent of the planned schedule elapsed, which is within the acceptable variance threshold established by Finance. Detailed figures are attached in the usual tracker for anyone who wants to review line items.

The one area I want to bring to everyone's attention is the vendor dependency with Calloway Systems for the API gateway component. Their delivery was originally slated for March 4 but has slipped to March 19 due to what they describe as an internal resourcing conflict on their end. This has a knock-on effect for our integration testing window, and I have asked Renata Silva to model out the impact on the overall Phase 2 end date. Renata, can you have that ready before Thursday's steering committee call so we can discuss mitigation options, including whether we pull forward any of the Phase 3 prep work to absorb the delay without slipping the go-live date.

Please review the attached slide deck for the full detail and come prepared with questions for Thursday's call. As always, if there is anything you need escalated before then, reach out directly rather than waiting for the weekly cycle.

Regards,
Marcus

---

From: Renata Silva
To: Marcus Feldman; Project Meridian Distribution List
Sent: Tuesday, March 11, 2:47 PM
Subject: RE: Meridian Phase 2 — Weekly Status Update (Week 11)

Marcus,

Thanks for the summary. I have started the impact analysis on the Calloway delay and expect to have a first draft ready by Wednesday afternoon so there is time for a quick review before Thursday's call. Initial read is that the two-week slip is absorbable if we shift the integration testing start date rather than the end date, but that compresses our regression testing window from three weeks down to two, which the QA lead, Tomas Reyes, has already flagged as tight but not unreasonable given the scope of changes in this release.

One additional consideration: if we do compress the regression window, I would recommend we deprioritize the optional performance benchmarking tasks that were added to the Phase 2 backlog in February and push those into Phase 3 instead. This would free up roughly thirty hours of QA capacity that could be redirected toward core regression coverage. I know this was a lower priority item originally requested by the Reporting team, so I want to make sure we get their buy-in before finalizing anything. Marcus, could you loop in Sandra Wu from Reporting so we can confirm this doesn't create a downstream problem for her team's deliverables?

I'll circulate the full model with scenarios A, B, and C by end of day Wednesday.

Best,
Renata

---

From: Sandra Wu
To: Renata Silva; Marcus Feldman; Project Meridian Distribution List
Sent: Tuesday, March 11, 4:02 PM
Subject: RE: Meridian Phase 2 — Weekly Status Update (Week 11)

Hi both,

Thanks for flagging this. The performance benchmarking work was intended to give us an early read on report generation times ahead of the fiscal year-end close, but it is not a hard dependency for the Phase 2 go-live itself. I am comfortable deferring it to Phase 3 provided we have confirmation that it will be completed no later than mid-May, since that gives us enough runway to validate before the June reporting cycle.

I would appreciate being included in Thursday's call if there is time allotted to discuss this specific item, mainly so I can confirm the revised timeline works for my stakeholders on the Finance reporting side. Otherwise, happy to proceed on the assumption above.

Thanks,
Sandra

From: Denise Halloran
To: Project Meridian Distribution List
Sent: Tuesday, March 4, 9:12 AM
Subject: Meridian Status Update - Week of March 3

Team,

Following up on last week's steering committee meeting, I wanted to circulate a summary of where things stand on the Meridian data migration workstream before our Thursday check-in. Overall we remain on track for the phase two cutover date of April 18, though there are a couple of items I want to flag early rather than let them surprise anyone later.

The reconciliation scripts for the legacy Vantage records are about 80% complete. Priya's team finished the customer master file validation last Thursday and found a smaller-than-expected discrepancy rate, roughly 1.4% of records requiring manual review, which is well within the tolerance we agreed on with Finance back in January. The remaining 20% covers the vendor and contract tables, which have more complex foreign key relationships, so I'd expect that work to wrap by March 14 rather than the original March 10 target. This is a three business day slip, not something I think warrants escalation, but I wanted it on the record.

On the infrastructure side, the staging environment refresh that IT Ops promised for last Friday actually landed Monday afternoon, which pushed our load testing window back slightly. Marcus has already rescheduled the test slots with the performance team and we're still comfortable hitting the March 21 sign-off gate. If anyone on this thread has visibility into why the refresh slipped, it would help for planning purposes going forward, but this isn't blocking anything critical right now.

One open item that does need a decision: the data retention policy question for the archived support tickets. Legal came back with guidance that anything older than seven years should be purged rather than migrated, but that conflicts with what Product had assumed when they scoped the historical reporting dashboard. I've put this on Thursday's agenda as a discussion item. If you have strong opinions either way, please come prepared, because we need to close this out before the vendor table reconciliation finishes so we know whether to build the purge logic into that same script pass.

Please let me know if you have questions before Thursday. Otherwise see everyone at 10am.

Denise

---

From: Marcus Delgado
To: Project Meridian Distribution List
Sent: Tuesday, March 4, 11:47 AM
Subject: RE: Meridian Status Update - Week of March 3

Adding a bit of color on the staging refresh delay since Denise mentioned it. IT Ops confirmed the holdup was related to a firmware patch on the storage array that had to be applied before they could provision the new volumes. Apparently this wasn't communicated to us ahead of time because the patch was originally scheduled for the following week and got pulled forward due to a vendor security advisory. Nothing alarming, just a scheduling miss on their side that they've acknowledged.

Load testing is now booked for March 17 through March 19, with a buffer day on the 20th in case we need to rerun anything. I've also asked the performance team to include a scenario that simulates the higher transaction volume we saw during the Q4 peak, since that wasn't part of the original test plan and I think it's worth having the data point even though it's not strictly required for sign-off.

Separately, a small housekeeping note: the shared drive folder for test scripts got reorganized last week without much warning, so if anyone's bookmarks are broken, the new structure mirrors the naming convention we use in the Atlas project, just under a Meridian parent folder this time. Reach out if you can't find something.

Marcus

---

From: Priya Nandakumar
To: Project Meridian Distribution List
Sent: Tuesday, March 4, 2:03 PM
Subject: RE: Meridian Status Update - Week of March 3

Thanks Denise, that summary matches what my team has been tracking. One clarification on the vendor and contract table timeline: the complexity isn't so much the foreign key relationships themselves as it is the number of tables that reference a "primary vendor" field that was apparently repurposed at some point in 2019 to also store internal cost center codes for a subset of records. We're having to write additional logic to distinguish which rows fall into which category before we can map them cleanly into the new schema. Rina found this while doing spot checks and it's a good catch, but it does add a bit of unplanned work.

I don't think this changes the March 14 estimate, but I wanted to explain the "why" in case it comes up in the steering committee readout. We'll have a clearer picture by end of day Wednesday once Rina finishes categorizing the affected rows, and I'll send a quick update either way so nobody is left wondering.

On the retention policy question, my instinct is that we should default to Legal's guidance and treat the reporting dashboard requirement as a separate conversation about whether Product needs a summarized or aggregated version of the old tickets rather than the raw records themselves. That might resolve the apparent conflict without either side having to fully back down. Happy to discuss more on Thursday.

Priya

From: Marcus Fenwick
To: Project Halcyon Distribution List
Subject: Weekly Status Update – Halcyon Migration, Week 14
Date: Tuesday, 9:14 AM

Good morning everyone,

Ahead of Thursday's steering committee meeting, I wanted to circulate a summary of where things stand with the Halcyon data migration workstream. Overall progress remains on track against the revised timeline, though we continue to see some friction in the reconciliation phase for the legacy customer records originating from the Brindlewood acquisition.

The ETL pipeline rebuild that Priya's team completed last sprint has reduced batch processing time from roughly six hours to just under ninety minutes, which is a meaningful improvement and should help us stay within the maintenance window agreed with Operations. That said, we are still seeing a non-trivial number of records fail validation on the address normalization step, particularly for accounts with international billing addresses. Devon has flagged this to the vendor and we are waiting on a response regarding whether this is a known limitation of the normalization library or something we need to patch ourselves.

On the infrastructure side, the new staging environment in the Ashford data center is fully provisioned and the network team has confirmed connectivity to both the legacy mainframe gateway and the new Postgres cluster. We did have a brief outage last Thursday when a firmware update on one of the switches caused a routing issue, but that was resolved within about forty minutes and did not affect any customer-facing systems.

Budget-wise, we are currently tracking about four percent under the revised Q3 forecast, mostly due to the delay in bringing on the second contractor from Meridian Consulting, whose start date has now been pushed to the 22nd. I'll have an updated burn-down chart ready for Thursday.

Please let me know if there's anything you'd like added to the agenda before then.

Best,
Marcus

---

From: Priya Chandrasekaran
To: Marcus Fenwick; Project Halcyon Distribution List
Subject: RE: Weekly Status Update – Halcyon Migration, Week 14
Date: Tuesday, 10:02 AM

Thanks for pulling this together, Marcus. A small correction on the batch processing numbers — the ninety-minute figure reflects the average across the last five runs, but our worst-case run last Friday actually took closer to two hours and ten minutes due to contention with the nightly backup job on the same cluster. I don't think this changes the overall picture much, but I wanted the committee to have the accurate range rather than just the average, especially since Operations may ask about worst-case scenarios given the maintenance window constraints.

On the address normalization issue, I spoke briefly with Devon yesterday and it sounds like the vendor's support team has acknowledged the ticket but hasn't given us a timeline yet. In the meantime, we've written a temporary workaround that flags the failing records for manual review rather than blocking the entire batch, which at least lets us keep moving on the records that do pass validation. It's not a long-term fix, but it unblocks about eighty percent of the Brindlewood accounts for now.

One additional item for Thursday's agenda: I'd like five minutes to walk through the proposed schema changes for the contact preferences table, since a couple of downstream teams have asked about how opt-in status will be represented after the migration. I know this was discussed briefly in Week 10, but there have been some tweaks since then based on feedback from the Compliance team.

Thanks,
Priya

From: Devon Alcaraz
To: Priya Chandrasekaran; Marcus Fenwick; Project Halcyon Distribution List
Subject: RE: Weekly Status Update – Halcyon Migration, Week 14

Just to close the loop on the vendor ticket — I heard back about twenty minutes ago. Support confirmed this is a known issue with the current version of the normalization library when handling addresses that include non-Latin characters in the street name field, which explains why it's disproportionately affecting the Brindlewood accounts given their customer base in the Benelux region. They're recommending we upgrade to version 4.3, which apparently includes a rewritten parser, but they can't commit to a release date for the patch that specifically addresses our reported edge cases. I'll follow up with our account rep to see if there's any flexibility there, but for now I think Priya's manual review workaround is the right call.

Separately, I wanted to flag that the QA team has requested an extra two days for regression testing on the reporting module, since the last test cycle turned up a handful of discrepancies in how subtotal rounding is calculated for multi-currency invoices. Nothing alarming, but they'd rather not rush it given how visible that report is to Finance. I don't think this affects the overall migration timeline, but it may push the reporting sign-off to Monday instead of Friday.

I can join Thursday's meeting a few minutes late if needed — I have a dentist appointment in the morning that's run a bit long in the past.

Devon

**scikit-learn** is a Python module for machine learning built on top of
SciPy and is distributed under the 3-Clause BSD license.

The project was started in 2007 by David Cournapeau as a Google Summer
of Code project, and since then many volunteers have contributed. See
the `About us <https://scikit-learn.org/dev/about.html#authors>`__ page
for a list of core contributors.

It is currently maintained by a community of contributors, with volunteers but also `support from several
organisations <https://scikit-learn.org/dev/institutional_support.html>`__.

Website: https://scikit-learn.org

Installation
------------

Dependencies
~~~~~~~~~~~~

scikit-learn requires:

- Python (>= |PythonMinVersion|)
- NumPy (>= |NumPyMinVersion|)
- SciPy (>= |SciPyMinVersion|)
- Narwhals (>= |NarwhalsMinVersion|)
- joblib (>= |JoblibMinVersion|)
- threadpoolctl (>= |ThreadpoolctlMinVersion|)

=======

Scikit-learn plotting capabilities (i.e., functions start with ``plot_`` and
classes end with ``Display``) require Matplotlib (>= |MatplotlibMinVersion|).
For running the examples Matplotlib >= |MatplotlibMinVersion| is required.
A few examples require scikit-image >= |Scikit-ImageMinVersion|, a few examples
require pandas >= |PandasMinVersion|, some examples require seaborn >=
|SeabornMinVersion| and Plotly >= |PlotlyMinVersion|.

User installation
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

If you already have a working installation of NumPy and SciPy,
the easiest way to install scikit-learn is using ``pip``::

    pip install -U scikit-learn

or ``conda``::

    conda install -c conda-forge scikit-learn

The documentation includes more detailed `installation instructions <https://scikit-learn.org/stable/install.html>`_.

This memorandum summarizes the terms and considerations associated with the renewal of the vendor services agreement between Halbrook Logistics Group and Corestone Supply Partners, effective for the twelve-month period beginning March 1 and concluding the last day of February of the following year. The purpose of this document is to provide an overview of the renewal discussion, the changes to pricing and service levels since the prior agreement, and the internal approvals required before the contract can be executed by both parties.

Corestone Supply Partners has served as Halbrook Logistics Group's primary vendor for warehouse packaging materials, palletizing equipment maintenance, and related consumable supplies since the initial agreement was signed three years ago. Over that period, the relationship has been managed on the Halbrook side by Denise Okafor, Director of Procurement, with day-to-day coordination handled by Marcus Feldt in the Operations department. On the Corestone side, the primary point of contact has been Rebecca Linden, Senior Account Manager, supported by Tom Grissom in Corestone's logistics coordination team. Both parties have expressed general satisfaction with the working relationship, and no material disputes or service failures were recorded during the most recent contract term, aside from a minor delay in Q3 shipment of stretch wrap film, which was resolved within the contractually allowed window and did not result in any penalty assessment.

As part of the renewal negotiation, Corestone proposed a 3.2 percent increase in unit pricing across the standard packaging materials category, citing increased costs of raw resin inputs and elevated freight surcharges affecting their own supply chain. Halbrook's procurement team reviewed this request against current market benchmarks obtained from two comparable vendors, Ashgrove Packaging Solutions and Deniston Industrial Supply, and determined that the proposed increase was within a reasonable range, falling slightly below the average increase reported by competitors during the same period. After a brief round of negotiation, Corestone agreed to cap the increase at 2.75 percent for the first six months of the renewed term, with the remaining 0.45 percent taking effect at the midpoint of the contract, contingent on no significant volatility in resin pricing during that window. This staged approach was proposed by Rebecca Linden as a way to ease the transition for Halbrook's budgeting cycle, and Denise Okafor confirmed that this structure aligns with the finance department's preference for predictable quarterly cost adjustments.

In addition to pricing, the renewal includes several updates to the service level agreement. The standard delivery window for routine orders has been reduced from five business days to four business days, a change requested by Halbrook's operations team following feedback from the Dallas and Reno distribution centers regarding inventory turnover constraints. Corestone has agreed to this adjustment without additional charge, noting that recent investments in their regional distribution hub in Oklahoma City have created sufficient capacity to support the shortened window without disrupting service to their other clients. The renewal also formalizes a quarterly business review meeting, to be held via video conference, during which both parties will review fill rates, on-time delivery percentages, and any emerging supply chain risks. This formal review process was not part of the original agreement and represents an enhancement suggested by Marcus Feldt after an internal audit recommended more structured vendor oversight across all major supply relationships.

The renewal agreement also addresses the equipment maintenance component of the contract, specifically the quarterly servicing of the automated palletizing units at the Reno facility. Corestone will continue to provide this service under the existing terms, with technician visits scheduled for the second week of each quarter. Halbrook's facilities team has requested that Corestone provide advance notice of at least ten business days prior to each scheduled visit, an adjustment from the previous seven-day notice requirement, to allow for better coordination with the facility's production schedule. Corestone has accepted this change without objection.

From a contractual standponing, the renewal document retains the same termination clause structure as the prior agreement, allowing either party to terminate with ninety days written notice, and it preserves the existing confidentiality and data handling provisions related to shared inventory forecasts and order history. Legal review of the renewal draft was completed by Halbrook's internal counsel, Priya Nandakumar, who confirmed that no substantive changes to liability or indemnification language were introduced in this renewal cycle. Corestone's legal team similarly confirmed no objections to the retained language during their review.

Before the renewal can be finalized, the agreement requires sign-off from Halbrook's Vice President of Operations, Gregory Ashcombe, as well as confirmation from the finance department that the revised pricing structure has been incorporated into the upcoming fiscal year budget projections. Denise Okafor has indicated that she expects to have both approvals in hand within the next two weeks, at which point the finalized agreement will be routed to Corestone for countersignature. Assuming no delays in this process, the renewed contract is expected to be fully executed before the current agreement's expiration date, ensuring continuity of service without any gap in coverage for packaging materials or scheduled equipment maintenance.

Overall, this renewal reflects a continuation of a stable and functional vendor relationship, with modest pricing adjustments, incremental service level improvements, and enhanced oversight mechanisms that should benefit both parties over the coming contract term. A follow-up summary will be circulated to relevant stakeholders once final signatures have been obtained.

Hi all,

Attaching the updated status summary for the Meridian Data Migration project, week 14. Overall we remain on track for the phase two cutover date of October 3rd, though there are a couple of items I want to flag before Thursday's steering committee call.

The ETL validation scripts for the customer master file are now passing at 98.7% reconciliation against the legacy Boru systems output. The remaining 1.3% discrepancy has been traced to a formatting issue in the regional tax identifier field for accounts originating from the Palmerston branch office. Denise's team is looking into whether this is a source data quality issue or a mapping logic gap on our side. We expect a resolution by end of day Wednesday, which should not impact the go-live timeline.

On the infrastructure side, the staging environment refresh completed successfully over the weekend. CPU and memory utilization during the batch load test stayed within expected thresholds, though we did see a longer-than-anticipated runtime on the nightly reconciliation job — approximately 45 minutes over the baseline. Tom, can you loop in the DBA team to see if this is related to the new indexing strategy we applied last sprint, or if it's simply a function of the larger data volume in this environment?

From a resourcing standpoint, we are still short one QA analyst following Renee's departure last month. HR has two candidates in the pipeline, and Priya is coordinating final interviews for early next week. In the meantime, Sanjay has agreed to backfill some of the regression testing duties, which we appreciate, though I want to make sure this doesn't create a bottleneck heading into UAT.

Please review the attached deck ahead of Thursday and send me any corrections or additions by end of day Wednesday so I can consolidate before the steering committee meeting.

Thanks,
Marcus

From: Denise Whitfield
To: Marcus Feldman; Priya Anand; Tom Kowalczyk; Sanjay Rao
Subject: RE: Meridian Data Migration – Weekly Status (Week 14)

Marcus,

Quick update on the tax identifier discrepancy — we found the root cause. The Palmerston branch records were exported using an older version of the Boru extraction utility that truncates the identifier field to eight characters instead of ten. This appears to have been introduced when the branch upgraded their local reporting tool back in March but never flagged to central IT. We've confirmed with the vendor that the field length issue is isolated to records extracted after that date, which narrows the affected population to roughly 4,200 accounts.

The fix itself is straightforward on our end — we'll adjust the mapping logic to pad and flag these records for manual review rather than silently truncating further. I've asked Oscar to prepare a small patch for the transformation layer, and we should have it ready for testing by Tuesday. I don't anticipate this pushing the October 3rd date, but wanted to make sure everyone has visibility given it touches the customer master file specifically.

Separately, on the QA staffing point — Sanjay, if it's easier, we can shift some of the lower-priority regression scripts to next sprint so you're not stretched too thin during the tax ID retesting. Let me know what works.

Best,
Denise

Prepared for the Executive Leadership Team of Halden & Marsh Consolidated Industries, this report summarizes operational and financial performance for the third quarter of the fiscal year, covering the period of July 1 through September 30. The information contained herein was compiled by the Office of Corporate Planning under the direction of Regional Operations Director Colin Aldrich, with contributions from the Finance, Logistics, and Human Resources departments. This document is intended for internal distribution only and should be reviewed alongside the supplementary spreadsheets circulated separately by the Finance team.

Overall, the quarter was characterized by steady, if unspectacular, performance across most business units. Consolidated revenue for the quarter reached approximately 14.2 million dollars, representing a 2.6 percent increase over the previous quarter and a 4.1 percent increase over the same period last year. This growth was driven primarily by continued momentum in the Northfield Distribution Division, which benefited from the completion of the Ashworth Logistics Upgrade Project earlier in the spring. That project, which involved the replacement of aging conveyor systems at the Millbrook Distribution Center, appears to have reduced average order fulfillment times by roughly eleven percent, a change that has translated into modest but measurable improvements in customer retention metrics tracked by the Client Services team.

The Manufacturing Division, led by Plant Operations Manager Denise Okafor, reported production output broadly in line with targets set during the spring planning cycle. Unit output at the Carrowgate facility increased slightly, from 218,400 units in the second quarter to 221,750 units in the third, while the Bellmont facility experienced a minor dip attributed to scheduled maintenance downtime during the first two weeks of August. This downtime had been anticipated in the annual maintenance calendar and did not materially affect the division's ability to meet outstanding customer orders. Raw material costs remained relatively stable during the quarter, though the Procurement team noted a slight uptick in freight surcharges associated with imported polymer components, a trend that is being monitored closely given ongoing volatility in shipping markets.

On the sales and business development front, the Client Accounts group, under the supervision of Senior Account Manager Priya Ramanathan, closed fourteen new contracts during the quarter, six of which fall under the mid-market segment and eight under the enterprise segment. Notable among these was the renewal and expansion of the service agreement with Thornfield Regional Retailers, a longstanding client whose contract now includes an additional distribution lane connecting the Southbridge warehouse to their newly opened retail locations in the tri-county area. The sales pipeline for the fourth quarter appears healthy, with approximately 3.4 million dollars in prospective contract value currently under active negotiation, though it should be noted that historical conversion rates suggest that not all of this figure will materialize into signed agreements.

Human Resources reported a relatively stable quarter with respect to staffing levels. Total headcount across all divisions stood at 1,042 employees as of September 30, a modest increase from 1,021 at the close of the previous quarter. This growth is largely attributable to the onboarding of new warehouse associates at the Southbridge facility in anticipation of increased seasonal volume expected in the fourth quarter. Voluntary turnover remained within the range considered normal for the industry, at approximately 3.8 percent for the quarter, though the Talent Retention Committee, chaired by HR Director Marcus Whitfield, has continued its review of exit interview data to identify any emerging patterns that might warrant further attention heading into the next fiscal year.

The Finance Department, under the direction of Controller Elena Vasquez, reported that operating expenses remained within budgeted parameters for the quarter, with total operating costs at approximately 11.6 million dollars. This figure includes routine expenditures related to facilities maintenance, utilities, insurance premiums, and administrative overhead. Gross margin for the quarter came in at 18.3 percent, a slight improvement over the 17.9 percent recorded in the prior quarter, attributable in part to the fulfillment efficiencies described earlier as well as modest reductions in per-unit shipping costs negotiated with the company's primary freight carrier, Redwing Transport Solutions. The Finance team has flagged the upcoming renewal of the company's general liability insurance policy, scheduled for early in the fourth quarter, as an item requiring attention from senior leadership given anticipated premium increases across the industry.

Looking ahead, the Corporate Planning Office anticipates that the fourth quarter will bring typical seasonal increases in order volume, particularly within the Northfield Distribution Division, and preparations are already underway to ensure adequate staffing and inventory levels to accommodate this expected demand. The planned rollout of the updated inventory management software at the Southbridge and Millbrook facilities remains on schedule for a mid-November implementation, and the IT Department, led by Systems Manager Gregory Ashton, has indicated that staff training sessions will begin in late October to ensure a smooth transition. Leadership will continue to monitor freight and raw material cost trends closely, and further updates will be provided in the year-end report scheduled for distribution in early January. Questions regarding the contents of this report may be directed to the Office of Corporate Planning during regular business hours.

From: Marcus Feld
To: Project Meridian Distribution List
Subject: Weekly Status Update – Meridian Data Migration, Week 14

Team,

Attached is the summary of progress for the week ending June 6th on the Meridian Data Migration initiative. Overall we remain on track for the phase two cutover date of July 15th, though there are a couple of items that need attention before we can consider the schema validation work fully closed out.

The ETL pipeline rebuild for the customer master records has completed its second round of testing. Priya's team ran the reconciliation scripts against the staging environment over the weekend and reported a 99.4% match rate against the legacy system output. The remaining discrepancies appear to be related to trailing whitespace in the legacy address fields, which is a known issue we flagged back in April. Devon is going to confirm with the Vendor Support desk at Calloway Systems whether their export utility can be configured to strip that automatically, or whether we need to handle it on our end with an additional transformation step.

On the infrastructure side, the new database cluster in the East region is provisioned and passed its initial load test on Thursday. CPU utilization stayed under 40% during the simulated peak, which gives us some comfort around headroom for the Q3 volume increase Finance mentioned in their forecast. I'd still like someone from the DBA team to double check the backup retention settings before we finalize, since the current config defaults to 14 days and our data governance policy requires 30 for anything touching customer PII.

One outstanding risk I want to flag for visibility: the vendor integration with Northgate Analytics is still pending their side of the API key rotation. We submitted the request on May 28th and haven't heard back beyond an automated acknowledgment. If this isn't resolved by June 13th, it will start to threaten the July 15th date, since QA needs at least a week with live-equivalent data before sign-off. I'll follow up directly with our account rep, Sandra Wu, this week and copy Elaine in Procurement in case escalation through the contract is needed.

Please review the attached burn-down chart and let me know if your workstream status differs from what's reflected there. As always, happy to take questions live in Thursday's standup.

Best,
Marcus

---

From: Priya Anand
To: Marcus Feld; Project Meridian Distribution List
Subject: RE: Weekly Status Update – Meridian Data Migration, Week 14

Marcus, thanks for the summary. Quick addition from my side on the reconciliation work — we also found a handful of records (around 60 total) where the legacy system had duplicate customer IDs pointing to two different account histories. This wasn't something we anticipated in the original data profiling, and it's a bit more involved than the whitespace issue since it touches on data integrity rather than formatting.

I don't think this is a blocker for the July date, but I do want to make sure we have a documented resolution process before UAT starts, otherwise the testers are going to flag every one of these as a defect and we'll spend cycles triaging something we already understand. I'm proposing we treat these as a known-issues list that gets reviewed with Compliance, since a couple of the duplicates involve accounts that were merged after a prior acquisition and may have specific handling requirements from a records-retention standpoint.

Can we get 20 minutes on Thursday's agenda to walk through this before the broader standup? I'd rather not surprise the group with it cold.

Priya

---

From: Devon Okafor
To: Priya Anand; Marcus Feld; Project Meridian Distribution List
Subject: RE: Weekly Status Update – Meridian Data Migration, Week 14

Happy to take the first 20 minutes for that, Priya, no objection from me. I'll shift the infra update to later in the agenda so it doesn't get squeezed.

Following up on the whitespace question from Marcus's note — I spoke with the Calloway Systems support desk yesterday afternoon. They confirmed their export utility does have a "trim whitespace" flag but it's only available in version 4.3 of their software, and we're currently licensed for 4.1. They quoted a modest upgrade fee, but more importantly the timeline for provisioning the new license through their portal is listed as 5 to 7 business days, which should still fit within our window if we submit the request today. I'll get that started and loop in Elaine so it's tracked alongside the Northgate item, since both are technically vendor dependencies at this point.

Separately, on the backup retention setting Marcus mentioned — I checked with Raj on the DBA team and he confirmed the 14-day default was left over from the template used to spin up the cluster, not an intentional choice. He's updating it to 30 days today and will send a screenshot of the confirmed setting for the audit trail once it's done.

Devon

---

From: Elaine Torres
To: Devon Okafor; Priya Anand; Marcus Feld; Project Meridian Distribution List
Subject: RE: Weekly Status Update – Meridian Data Migration, Week 14

Thanks, all. Noting both vendor items on my end — Calloway license upgrade and the Northgate API key rotation. I'll reach out to our contract manager for Northgate today to see if there's a service-level clause we can point to, since five business days without any substantive response is outside what I'd expect given the support terms in that agreement. I'll report back before Thursday so we have something concrete to discuss if escalation ends up being necessary.

On an unrelated note, Finance asked me to remind the group that any additional licensing costs, including the Calloway upgrade fee Devon mentioned, need to route through the standard purchase request form before we commit, even if the amount is small. I know this has come up before, but I wanted to mention it again since we have two vendor items moving at once this week. Happy to walk anyone through the form if it's been a while.

See everyone Thursday.

Elaine

Ticket #48213-A
Account: Merrow Blane Textiles Ltd.
Submitted by: D. Farraday (Accounts Administrator)
Assigned Support Rep: T. Osei, Tier 2 Support
Priority: Standard
Status: Resolved

Initial submission, 09:14, March 3rd: Customer reports that the monthly invoice export function within the Ledgerhouse Cloud platform is generating files with truncated line items whenever the export exceeds 500 rows. Customer states this issue began appearing after the most recent platform update (version 6.14.2) was pushed to their account on February 28th. Attached to the ticket is a sample CSV file showing the truncation occurring at row 501, with the remaining 42 rows simply omitted from the export. Customer notes this is affecting their month-end reconciliation process and requests expedited review given the proximity to their internal reporting deadline of March 10th.

Response logged 10:47, March 3rd, T. Osei: Acknowledged receipt of ticket and attached file. Confirmed reproduction of the issue on an internal test account configured with a similarly sized dataset. Escalating to engineering team for further investigation. Advised customer that a workaround is available in the interim: exports can be split into smaller batches using the date-range filter under the Export Settings panel, which should allow full data retrieval until a permanent fix is implemented. Customer acknowledged workaround at 11:20 and stated they would attempt it for the current cycle.

Update logged 14:32, March 3rd, D. Farraday: Customer confirms the batch export workaround functioned correctly for a test run of 200 rows but reports that the interface becomes unresponsive when attempting to export a second batch immediately afterward without refreshing the browser session. Customer asks whether this is expected behavior or a separate issue that should be logged independently.

Response logged 15:05, March 3rd, T. Osei: Clarified that the browser refresh requirement is a known limitation of the current export module and not related to the truncation bug, though it will be noted internally as a secondary usability issue for future review. Advised customer to refresh the session between batch exports as a temporary measure. No additional ticket opened at this time, as the behavior is considered low-impact relative to the primary issue.

Internal note, 09:02, March 4th, T. Osei: Engineering has replied to escalation. Root cause identified as a regression introduced in version 6.14.2 related to a change in the pagination logic for the export query. Fix is being tested internally and is tentatively scheduled for inclusion in patch 6.14.3, expected to be released within five to seven business days. Flagging this ticket as pending engineering resolution.

Update logged 09:40, March 4th, T. Osei: Contacted customer to relay engineering's findings. Informed D. Farraday that a patch is in progress and provided the estimated release window. Reiterated that the batch export workaround remains available in the meantime. Customer expressed some concern regarding the timeline given their March 10th deadline but agreed the workaround was sufficient to proceed for the current reporting cycle.

Update logged 16:15, March 6th, D. Farraday: Customer follows up requesting confirmation of patch status, noting that the reconciliation deadline is now four days away. Customer also asks whether historical export files generated between February 28th and March 3rd may have been silently truncated without their knowledge, and requests guidance on how to verify this.

Response logged 08:55, March 7th, T. Osei: Advised customer that any exports generated during the affected window exceeding 500 rows should be manually spot-checked against the account's transaction ledger totals to confirm completeness. Provided a brief set of instructions for cross-referencing row counts using the built-in ledger summary tool under Reports > Reconciliation Summary. Informed customer that engineering has confirmed the fix has passed internal QA and is now scheduled for deployment on March 8th, ahead of the original estimate.

Update logged 11:30, March 8th, T. Osei: Patch 6.14.3 deployed to customer's account as part of the scheduled release. Internal test export of 542 rows completed successfully with no truncation observed. Notified customer of the deployment and requested they verify on their end at their earliest convenience.

Update logged 13:47, March 8th, D. Farraday: Customer confirms successful export of a full dataset totaling 617 rows with no truncation. Thanks support team for the timely resolution and workaround guidance provided throughout the process. Customer also confirms that the earlier concern regarding potentially truncated historical exports was resolved upon manual review; all figures reconciled correctly against the ledger summary, and no discrepancies were found.

Internal note, 14:10, March 8th, T. Osei: Customer-reported issue confirmed resolved via patch 6.14.3. No further action required from engineering on this specific ticket. Noting for internal tracking that the secondary usability issue regarding session refresh between batch exports remains open as a low-priority item and has been forwarded to the product team for consideration in a future release cycle, separate from this ticket.

Closing note, 09:15, March 9th, T. Osei: Ticket marked as resolved following customer confirmation and no further correspondence received within the standard 24-hour follow-up window. Customer satisfaction survey sent per standard procedure. Case closed. Should the issue recur or the customer experience related symptoms, they have been advised to reference this ticket number when submitting a new request to expedite context review by support staff.

Follow-up note, 10:02, March 12th, D. Farraday: Customer sends brief message confirming that month-end reconciliation was completed on schedule with no further export issues encountered. No additional action requested. Ticket remains closed.

End of log.
